articles.title: Mudryk señala al responsable de su positivo por dopaje y confiesa que "pensé en suicidarme"
articles.standfirst: Mykhailo Mudryk, que estuvo 20 meses suspendido por dopaje, ha decidido contar toda su historia, incluidos sus momentos más oscuros
articles.summary: Mykhailo Mudryk, que estuvo 20 meses suspendido por dopaje, ha decidido contar toda su historia, incluidos sus momentos más oscuros
articles.body: Mykhailo Mudryk, extremo por el que el Chelsea pagó 100 millones de euros que juega cedido en el Tottenham y que fue considerado el peor fichaje de la historia del fútbol, responsabiliza a la dirección de la selección nacional de Ucrania de su control antidopaje positivo y de la consiguiente sanción que lo apartó del fútbol. El futbolista de 25 años fue suspendido desde noviembre de 2024 hasta julio de 2026 tras dar positivo por meldonium, una sustancia prohibida que; según él, esta entró en su organismo durante una concentración con su selección nacional. Aunque inicialmente la Federación Inglesa de Fútbol (FA) le impuso una sanción de cuatro años, su recurso ante el Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS) prosperó. Regresó al fútbol tras admitir que había infringido las normas antidopaje y aceptar una suspensión equivalente al tiempo que ya había cumplido. Mykhailo Mudryk fue claro cuando, durante una entrevista concedida al canal de YouTube ucraniano 'Guest of Gordon', le preguntaron directamente a quién culpaba de su sanción por dopaje: "Al entorno, a la situación en la selección nacional de Ucrania Eso nunca debería haber ocurrido. Probablemente no lo había dicho públicamente hasta ahora, pero lo digo ahora... ¿Si culpo directamente a la selección de Ucrania? Sí, exactamente". "Nunca había oído hablar de una sustancia como el meldonium. Es algo que solo se consigue en Europa del Este. Sólo pudo haber entrado en mi organismo estando en Ucrania. En Inglaterra no existe ese tipo de sustancia", explicó el futbolista, que sostiene que sólo había estado en Ucrania para acompañar a la selección nacional y que insistió en que "todo apunta a que ocurrió durante una concentración del equipo nacional". Mykhailo Mudryk fue un poco más lejos al asegurar que Andriy Shevchenko (presidente de la Asociación Ucraniana de Fútbol (UAF)) le brindó muy poco apoyo y responsabilizar a la UAF de las filtraciones que surgieron durante el proceso. "Fue algo totalmente inesperado. No podía creer que el resultado positivo fuera real. Fue como caer desde un rascacielos. En un sueño, uno llegaría a chocar contra el suelo; en la vida real, simplemente seguí cayendo. Me afectó muchísimo, a nivel mental", se sinceró. Mykhailo Mudryk confesó que lloró y consumió alcohol tras la suspensión, pero que nunca dudó de que terminaría regresando al fútbol de élite. "Pensé en suicidarme, pero enseguida me di cuenta de que esa no era la salida", se sinceró.

articles.title: Texans vs. Colts Thursday Night Football: How to Watch/Stream, Game Preview
articles.summary: Everything you need to know heading into the Houston Texans' primetime matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans are rallying for their Week 11 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts on a short week of preparation, as these two will have a primetime date on Thursday Night Football for their second meeting of the year.

The last time these two faced off, the Colts were the ones who got the edge, despite Houston dominating the turnover battle, 3-0-- which was the loss that ultimately dropped them to 0-3 after Week 3.

This week, the Texans simply can't afford to drop the ball again, as another loss would allow them to fall to 3-7, and might just be the nail in the coffin for their hopes of seeing their record make a comeback for a playoff run in the second half of the season.

Here's everything you need to know about the Texans' upcoming matchup against the Colts, including where to watch, betting lines, and more information:

What: Houston Texans vs. Indianapolis Colts in Week 11

Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change.

If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER.

OT Charlie Heck: QUESTIONABLE (personal)

LS Luke Rhodes: QUESTIONABLE (hamstring)

Can the Texans' defense recover without Azeez Al-Shaair?: News surfaced this week of the Texans placing Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair on injured reserve due to a groin injury that requires surgery. Houston's captain and green-dot signal caller will miss at least the next four weeks, and possibly more depending on how his recovery timeline looks. So can the Texans' defense rebound from such a loss? This game will be the second test to see whether or not they can do so. Henry To'oTo'o will act as Houston's new green-dot in the middle of the field-- according to DeMeco Ryans-- and Jake Hansen is likely to fill their other linebacker role. Time will tell if such a plan of attack will be enough.

How David Montgomery looks leading the backfield: Another name the Texans will be without in this game is their lead ball carrier in the running back room, Woody Marks, as he still sits in the middle of concussion protocol. But Houston will have David Montgomery in the lineup for the first time since Week 5. Montgomery hasn't performed particularly well when he's been on the field this season. He hasn't scored a touchdown since his hat trick performance in Week 1, and he's averaging just 2.7 yards per carry on the season. Expect to see him get a lot of work in the backfield against the Colts, but it remains to be seen how effective he looks with those extended opportunities.

Will Houston's penalty issues pop up once again?: It felt like the Texans' penalty issues had turned a corner in Week 9 against the LA Chargers as they incurred just six penalties for less than 40 yards en route to a dominant win. However, those concerns arose once again against the Browns as Houston recorded a whopping 13 penalties for over 100 yards given up. That's far from a recipe for success, and it's become a common trend for the Texans this season to fall into those frequent issues of lacking discipline and limiting flags. To ensure they can meet expectations for a one-sided victory against the Colts on Thursday, a large part of that relies on not getting behind so consistently when it comes to penalties.

articles.title: Manchester United: Drone footage of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session leaked online
articles.summary: A 12-minute video of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Manchester United boss has been leaked online, showing the new head coach doing training drills ahead of Sunday's match against Liverpool at Anfield, which is live on Sky
articles.body:
The 12-minute drone footage over their Carrington training ground was uploaded onto YouTube.

It shows Pochettino doing various tactical drills with his new team as they prepare for their clash with Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

United have signs around the Carrington area warning that use of drones are "strictly prohibited" and anyone caught "will be reported for prosecution and subject to civil action".

The uploaders of the drone footage, CC Overview, claimed to have not breached any laws.

On the video they posted: "For the people asking about legality. It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it, the drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn't fly over anyone or even near anyone so was a perfectly legal flight going by the CAA rules that regulates drone usage.

"The drone is correctly labelled and I hold all the relevant licences, public liability and insurance required.

"As for leaking team news/ tactics, it was half an hour into the manager's first training session, there are many media there so certainly won't be the only footage of training released."

The training today was a closed session and not open to the media.

Manchester United declined to comment when contacted by Sky Sports News .

Analysis: Leaked drone footage 'a significant tactical advantage to Liverpool'

"This 12-minute video starts off innocuously. We see large numbers of Man Utd players on a separate pitch doing what is known as rondos, those small groups of six or seven players with one or two in the middle trying to intercept the ball. It's the classic pre-training warm-up. That's pretty innocuous. That won't give Liverpool or anyone else much of an insight into what Pochettino's tactical thinking might be for his first game in charge.

"But then on the next pitch, as the drone moves across, it zooms in, and the zoom is quite incredible. You can make out faces and we see Pochettino hands-on, walking them through certain match scenarios. At one stage Pochettino calls all those players in for a huddle and a briefing.

"I'm not going to give you any information about who those players are. But these 11 players Pochettino calls in - 10 outfield players and one goalkeeper. We shouldn't assume this is his starting XI, necessarily.

"Saturday would be the day we'd expect United to do their specific tactics and shape to prepare for the game at Anfield the next day. If this was drone footage of that session it would be even more damaging, even more explosive.

"But the fact it's 11 players separated from the group... it's a very difficult situation for Pochettino and Manchester United.

"I don't think [Pochettino and the players] were aware of it at the time.

"It's questionable whether the person handling the drone has done anything illegal. All around Carrington training ground, they have a large numbers of signs up saying drones are prohibited. But it's clear from these images the drone was not flying directly above United's property. It was to the side of United's property and zoomed in.

"There's absolutely no suggestion Liverpool are involved in this, they are clearly not. But you have to say, it could be advantageous to Liverpool and Andoni Iraola if he's planning his tactics for Sunday's game to look at this and get an idea of how Manchester United might be lining up and what Pochettino might be thinking.

"While it seems as though there are probably no laws that have been broken here, nevertheless it's an awful lot of very specific footage which Manchester United and Pochettino would not want out in the public.

"If you look at the impact of what we're talking about, Man Utd earlier today released some images of the training session and it showed Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu among the main training group. Both of those have had injury concerns of late. So those official images told me, Man Utd supporters and Liverpool's tactical preparation experts that Maguire and Dorgu may be in line for possible selection.

"It's gone a stage further now with this leaked drone footage because that has shed even more light on that. It gives a pretty clear picture of who's fit, who's out on the training field, who's involved and who isn't.

"That has to be a significant tactical advantage to Andoni Iraola and Liverpool as they go into this huge game on Sunday."

Watch Liverpool vs Man Utd live on Sky Sports Premier League from 4pm on Sunday; kick-off 4.30pm

articles.title: Mykhailo Mudryk: Andriy Shevchenko disputes player's doping claims
articles.summary: Ukraine great Andriy Shevchenko accuses Mykhailo Mudryk of a "baseless slander" after the on-loan Tottenham winger blamed his failed drugs test on the nation's football association.
articles.body:
Ukraine great Andriy Shevchenko has accused Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives of repeatedly asking for an employee of the country's football federation to "falsely" take the blame for the winger's positive drugs test.

Tottenham winger Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan from Chelsea , was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium.

The 25-year-old said he blames the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban, believing it entered his system while on international duty.

In an interview on Wednesday, Mudryk firmly placed the blame for his 20-month absence from the sport on his national association, which has led to Shevchenko's response.

In a statement, former Chelsea and AC Milan striker Shevchenko, who is now president of the UAF, said Mudryk's comments amounted to a "baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally" and called on the player to retract his words.

He added: "His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample.

"The UAF refused, as such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work."

He added that "numerous investigations and audits" undertaken as part of the case were unable to shed light on when or where the substance entered Mudryk's system.

In his interview Mudryk also claimed Shevchenko had offered him little support, blamed the association for leaks that emerged during the case and said its handling of the matter delayed his return to football.

However, Shevchenko went on to say that national team staff had complied with a request from Chelsea not to provide Mudryk with any medication while on international duty.

And he also challenged the former Shakhtar Donetsk forward to provide evidence "to back up his words".

"Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps," Shevchenko added.

"These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine.

"The UAF completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk's representatives with the information they requested and remained in contact with those working on the case.

"I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism.

"If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question."

BBC Sport has contacted Mudryk's representatives for comment.

Mauricio Pochettino's first training session at Manchester United turned into an unexpectedly public affair.

articles.title: Arsenal Women 0-2 Lyon Women: Gunners' automatic Champions League qualification hopes hanging by a thread
articles.summary: Arsenal register a single shot on target, which came in stoppage-time, as they were outclassed by Lyon at Meadow Park; Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay scored in each half but the French side could easily have finished with more goals in what was a dominant performance
articles.body:
The French side, who beat Arsenal in the semi-finals last season, got the better of the Gunners again at Meadow Park on Thursday night with goals from Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay in each half sealing the victory.

Arsenal barely laid a glove on Lyon - who are yet to concede a goal in this season's Champions League - and now sit eighth in the standings, three points adrift of fourth-placed Chelsea, after their first loss in five league phase matches.

Emily Fox registered Arsenal's only shot on target of the game deep in stoppage-time and the home side could easily have conceded a few more had Marie-Antoinette Katoto not spurned two big opportunities.

Arsenal were also indebted to their goalkeeper, Misa, who produced three big saves in the second half to keep out Tabitha Chawinga, Dumornay and Vicki Becho.

Renee Slegers' side, now without a win in three matches in all competitions, are relying on teams above them to drop points in the final round of matches to avoid having to face a play-off match to secure their passage to the quarter-finals.

Meanwhile, Lyon, who currently sit second in the table, have secured a top-four finish with a game to spare after picking up 13 points from five matches.

Arsenal Women boss Renee Slegers to ESPN:

"Tough battle. Congratulations to Lyon who were better than us today. They play good football, physically strong in the duels, fast with the ball and without the ball.

"We had a tough time dealing with it in the first half. Second half we controlled the game better without creating clear-cut chances.

"But then you see how clinical Lyon were from their moments."

On her half-time team talk: "It was 1-0, so we were in the game. Like they had, we need moments as well. We are going to get moments and then how we are going to create it."

Sky Sports News reporter Uma Gurav at Meadow Park:

"The bigger picture here is that Arsenal have played the best two teams in this competition in two consecutive weeks and they've got just one point out of the two games.

"You have to admit the draw was very tough on them to get both Barcelona and Lyon, but it's also a harsh reality check.

"This Arsenal team won the Champions League just 18 months ago. Now, they're not quite up there with the European elites. Can they get back there anytime soon?"

Is it time to question Arsenal boss Slegers?

Ex-Arsenal striker Lianne Sanderson to ESPN:

"I like Renee but there has to come a time [when we question] why is it that all the players look out of form? Apart from Alessia Russo, how many of those players are actually performing?

"There has to come a point where you have to start questioning Renee. As much as I like Renee and everything she's done.

"Not to compare the two, but it feels like Michael Carrick at Man Utd where you feel like someone has taken the team so far but now what?

"We're all waiting for Arsenal to kick on. That tonight disappointed me because it looked flat."

articles.title: New FSU Coaching Rumors on Duke's Manny Diaz, Search for Mike Norvell's Replacement
articles.summary: Duke head coach Manny Diaz reportedly won't be filling Florida State's head coaching vacancy.
articles.body:
Duke head coach Manny Diaz reportedly won't be filling Florida State's head coaching vacancy.

According to Pete Nakos of On3.com, Diaz is staying at Duke despite being a "top candidate" in the Seminoles' search for a new head coach.

Florida State is looking for a full-time replacement for Mike Norvell, who was fired after the team dropped to 3-5 to begin the 2026 season. Rick Stockstill currently serves as the Seminoles' interim head coach.

Diaz has ties to Florida State. He graduated from the school with a bachelor's degree in communications in 1995. He also started his coaching career with the Seminoles, operating as a graduate assistant on their staff beginning in 1998.

Still, Diaz previously confirmed that he was content with remaining a member of the Blue Devils after leading them to a 25-12 record across his three seasons patrolling the sidelines.

"I addressed the team last night, I made it pretty clear, really, really happy here," Diaz said on Nov. 2, per Anna Snyder of the Fayetteville Observer . "Love being here, love going to work here every day. Anything we focus on other than finding a way to beat NC State is a distraction. Internet rumors are going to be Internet rumors. I told coaches and players we're the same, right? Everybody thinks our players are going to go somewhere else, right? So that's just the cost of success, which I'd rather have than the alternative."

Now, the Seminoles will continue the search for a new coach as they attempt to establish themselves as a threat in the ACC once again.

Nakos previously reported that Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann was also a candidate for the job opening, while former Florida State head coach Jimbo Fisher has been linked to the school as well.

articles.title: Un Atlético de película
articles.standfirst: El club convierte la Gran Vía en un ‘Broadway’ en rojiblanco para la presentación de 'Bien hecho'. Gil Marín, Cerezo, Simeone, los capitanes y leyendas desfilan por una alfombra única
articles.summary: El club convierte la Gran Vía en un ‘Broadway’ en rojiblanco para la presentación de 'Bien hecho'. Gil Marín, Cerezo, Simeone, los capitanes y leyendas desfilan por una alfombra única
articles.body: El Atlético de Madrid convirtió este jueves la Gran Vía en su particular Broadway en rojiblanco. ‘Bien hecho’ lucía en los rótulos del corazón de la capital de España para anunciar la presentación del documental producido por Atleti Studios y disponible en exclusiva en Movistar Plus que cuenta la extraordinaria historia de Javier García Pajares, aficionado rojiblanco que padece sordoceguera y que ha logrado superar numerosas barreras personales gracias a su actitud, resiliencia y afán de superación. En el interior del Palacio de la Prensa, la alfombra roja (y blanca) daba fe de que no se trataba de una simple presentación. Por allí desfiló la flor y nata del club, desde su consejero delegado, Miguel Ángel Gil y su presidente Enrique Cerezo a todos los estamentos del club: Simeone y su mujer Carla Pereyra, los cuatro capitanes (Koke, Oblak, Llorente y Barrios); el técnico del Femenino, David González, y las jugadoras Silvia Lloris, Lucía Rodríguez, Fiamma Benítez y Natalia Peñalvo; leyendas como Fernando Torres (y los capitanes de su Madrileño, Castillo, Sergio Díez, David Muñoz y Astralaga), Ruiz, Bermejo, Pedraza, Manolo y un David Villa también en su cargo de miembro del consejo de administración. No podía faltar nadie a un evento de Oscar. Tanto es así, que hasta 500 invitados se darían cita para ver una película inspiradora que a lo largo de sus 47 minutos (plenamente accesible, con subtítulos, audiodescripción y lengua de signos, reforzando su mensaje de inclusión y superación personal) encarna como pocas los valores de fortaleza, coraje y resiliencia que representan al aficionado rojiblanco. Por eso tampoco faltarían personalidades como Alfonso Gómez, CEO de Movistar Plus; Miguel Carballeda, presidente del Grupo Social ONCE o Alejandro Oñoro, CEO de Ilunion. Pese a que la historia de superación de Javier García Pajares trasciende lo deportivo, Enrique Cerezo aprovechó la ocasión para hacer un paralelismo con la temporada del Atlético, atreviéndose a sugerir títulos. “Se le podrían poner tantos... pero el mejor es ‘Vamos a ganar’”, señalaría. “Todas las competiciones serán muy difíciles, pero vamos a luchar por conseguir lo máximo posible”, añadió antes de dejar claro cómo terminará la película. “Con un final feliz, en nuestro campo y ganando la Champions sería lo perfecto”, zanjó. Koke también tomó el ejemplo del protagonista para empaparse de su lección de vida y trasladarla al verde. “Uno siempre se puede superar, que no hay que ponerse límites, que no hay que acomodarse con lo que uno tiene y hay que ir a por más”.

articles.title: Michigan Receiver Andrew Marsh is Facing a Misdemeanor Indecent Exposure Charge
articles.summary: PITTSFIELD TOWNSHIP, Mich. (AP) — Michigan receiver Andrew Marsh is facing a misdemeanor charge of indecent exposure after a food delivery driver alleged that he exposed himself to her after she dropped off his order.
articles.body:
PITTSFIELD TOWNSHIP, Mich. (AP) — Michigan receiver Andrew Marsh is facing a misdemeanor charge of indecent exposure after a food delivery driver alleged that he exposed himself to her after she dropped off his order.

Pittsfield Township Police released details of the incident from Feb. 1 in a social media post on Thursday. Marsh was charged last month by the Washtenaw County Prosecutor's Office and is set to appear for arraignment and pretrial proceedings on Dec. 2, according to police and court documents.

Police say they were contacted by the driver, who told them Marsh pulled aside a blanket and exposed his genitals to her as she turned to leave. Marsh sent a message to the driver stating she was attractive and asking her to return, according to the police statement.

An 18-year-old male at the address confirmed he was the recipient of the delivery, according to police. Indecent exposure in the state can carry a prison sentence of up to one year, a fine of up to $1,000 or both.

"We were just made aware of an incident involving Andrew Marsh," the school said in a statement sent to The Associated Press. "We will continue to monitor the situation as more information becomes available, but we are unable to comment further due to the ongoing case."

A message sent to Marsh's lawyer seeking comment was not immediately returned.

Marsh was listed as questionable on the Big Ten's availability report Wednesday ahead of the Wolverines' home game Saturday against unbeaten No. 4 UCLA .

Marsh, a sophomore from Texas, leads Michigan with 48 catches through 10 games. He has 459 yards and one touchdown reception in his second season with the team.

articles.title: Pina se divierte en el Johan Cruyff con su primer 'hat-trick' europeo
articles.standfirst: El Barcelona vuelve a pasar el rodillo y le endosa un set en blanco al Servette
articles.summary: El Barcelona vuelve a pasar el rodillo y le endosa un set en blanco al Servette
articles.body: Siete años y medio después de enlazar dos partidos seguidos sin ganar, el Barcelona se desquitó y volvió a pasar el rodillo por Europa. Tras la última goleada (0-8) ante el HB Køge, esta vez fue el Servette suizo el que se llevó un correctivo del Johan Cruyff. Y eso que le costó al equipo azulgrana entrar en el partido. En un arranque algo plano, no fue hasta el minuto 20 cuando Aitana anotó la primera ocasión clara, en un pase atrás de Claudia Pina que desvió ligeramente una rival. A partir de ese momento, se volvió a desatar el aluvión de goles. Las protagonistas del primer tanto se intercambiaron los papeles y Aitana sirvió en bandeja el segundo a Pina, en una gran triangulación dentro del área en la que también participó Serrajordi. Poco más de diez minutos bastaron para sentenciar el encuentro; un paradón de Weimar evitó el gol de Hansen y precedió al tanto de Brugts de cabeza en el córner a la media hora. El Servette acabó bien la primera mitad e incluso anotó un gol, anulado por fuera de juego desde el VAR. Tras la reanudación, Brugts se quedó cerca de celebrar su doblete, pero la revisión también demostró la posición adelantada de la neerlandesa. No obstante, cinco minutos después y a la hora de partido, siguió con su exhibición particular y provocó el penalti que supondría el cuarto del Barcelona, obra de Hansen; sexto gol en cinco partidos para la noruega. Inmediatamente después, Pere Romeu empezó a gestionar los descansos y retiró del campo a Aitana y a la propia Hansen, ambas autoras de gol y asistencia. El conjunto local manejó el partido, pero aún le dio tiempo para seguir aumentando la ventaja. Un gran pase por dentro de Serrajordi tras una combinación colectiva dejó sola delante de la portera a Claudia Pina, que cruzó el balón para hacer el quinto. Y cuando ya agonizaba el partido, la '9' del Barcelona aprovechó otro centro atrás de Brugts para hacer su 'hat-trick', -el primero en Champions-, y el sexto del equipo. Opacada por Pina, la lateral izquierdo azulgrana fue la otra figura; gol, asistencia, penalti provocado y otro tanto anulado. El Barcelona consiguió una nueva victoria abultada en Europa para seguir en todo lo alto de la clasificación, junto al intratable Lyonnes, y mantener el invicto en esta Champions League.

articles.title: Dos Mundiales en tres semanas: el insólito récord de dos adolescentes
articles.standfirst: El tayiko Komiljon Sharipov y el fiyiano Ryan Swami participan en el Mundial Sub-17 de Catar después de competir en Bakú en la categoría sub-15
articles.summary: El tayiko Komiljon Sharipov y el fiyiano Ryan Swami participan en el Mundial Sub-17 de Catar después de competir en Bakú en la categoría sub-15
articles.body: Mientras la Aspire Zone de Doha vive estos días el torneo que reúne a las 48 mejores selecciones Sub-17 del planeta, dos de sus protagonistas cargan con una etiqueta que no tiene nadie más sobre el césped: la de llevar dos Mundiales en el cuerpo con apenas unas semanas de diferencia. Komiljon Sharipov y Ryan Swami tienen 15 años, nacieron en 2011 y acaban de convertirse en los primeros futbolistas que disputan una Copa Mundial Sub-15 y una Sub-17 casi seguidas. Uno es tayiko; el otro, fiyiano. Y los dos están ahora mismo en Catar. El viaje arrancó en Bakú. A finales de octubre, la capital de Azerbaiyán estrenó la Copa Mundial y Festival Sub-15 de la FIFA, y allí coincidieron, sin saberlo, estos dos adolescentes de mundos opuestos. Para Sharipov, centrocampista, la cita terminó por todo lo alto: Tayikistán remontó un 1-0 y batió a Canadá en la final de su categoría, con dos goles y una asistencia suyos en el desenlace. “Íbamos por detrás y conseguimos darle la vuelta”, recuerda como su mejor instante del torneo. Para Swami, la experiencia tuvo el sabor agridulce de las selecciones modestas. Fiyi cayó goleada por Indonesia (7-1), pero el delantero firmó el único tanto de los suyos, un gol que se lleva grabado pese al marcador. “Poder jugar dos Mundiales y acumular tanta experiencia es una sensación extraordinaria”, confiesa, y añade la lección que se trajo de Azerbaiyán: la importancia de ser ordenado dentro del campo. Lo que los une no es solo la casualidad de las fechas, sino la rareza de su hazaña. Son los primeros que encadenan los dos grandes torneos juveniles de la FIFA en una misma ventana, y no como figurantes: llegan a Doha siendo ya internacionales con rodaje, chavales que han tenido que adaptarse a rivales, escenarios y presiones muy distintos antes de cumplir los dieciséis. En un torneo donde casi todos sus compañeros se estrenan en una cita mundial, ellos repiten. Para Swami, además, el calendario depara un examen de altura. Fiyi comparte el Grupo H con España, y el 23 de noviembre los isleños del Pacífico se miden a los de David Cubillo, una de las grandes favoritas y aspirante al único título que le falta al fútbol español. El delantero fiyiano podría así encontrarse, con 15 años y dos Mundiales a la espalda, frente a la cantera de un campeón del mundo. Detrás de esa precocidad asoma una estructura. La trayectoria de Sharipov es una de las vitrinas del Programa de Desarrollo del Talento que impulsa la FIFA bajo la batuta de Arsène Wenger, pensado para tender puentes entre el fútbol local y el profesional sin que el lugar de nacimiento o la economía familiar decidan quién llega. El tayiko se formó en la academia que el organismo tiene en su país, y Tayikistán —que ampliará su red con un nuevo centro en la región de Varzob— ya recoge frutos: varios de sus internacionales juveniles han salido de ahí. El relato tiene también su lado íntimo, el de dos adolescentes que se saben embajadores de lugares que rara vez aparecen en los titulares del fútbol. “Vestir la camiseta de mi selección es algo especial, me recuerda de dónde vengo”, dice Sharipov. Swami tira de los suyos para explicarlo: “Mucha gente me ha ayudado a llegar hasta aquí, pero mi padre y mi hermano me apoyan a diario. Jugar con Fiyi es como jugar para mi familia”.

articles.title: Las piernas del Madrid, bajo examen tras el parón
articles.standfirst: Los de Mou regresan con 1.905 minutos internacionales acumulados (8 goles y 9 asistencias), muchas horas de vuelo y varias estrellas exigidas al límite
articles.summary: Los de Mou regresan con 1.905 minutos internacionales acumulados (8 goles y 9 asistencias), muchas horas de vuelo y varias estrellas exigidas al límite
articles.body: El Real Madrid regresa a la competición después de un parón internacional que ha dejado una factura considerable en buena parte de su plantilla. A la acumulación de minutos de algunos de sus futbolistas se añade el desgaste de los desplazamientos. Vinicius y Endrick viajaron hasta Singapur con Brasil, o Valverde que tuvo que cruzar el Atlántico para incorporarse a Uruguay. Unos vuelos de muchas horas que reducen el margen de recuperación antes de volver a ponerse a las órdenes de José Mourinho. Un peaje añadido para las piernas justo antes de retomar la competición, con un calendario que no concede demasiado tiempo para recuperar. Con la Champions League de nuevo en el horizonte, el cuerpo técnico tendrá que gestionar el regreso de una plantilla que ha repartido buena parte de sus esfuerzos entre las selecciones. El Madrid ha acumulado 1.905 minutos internacionales en este parón (8 goles y 9 asistencias en total), una cifra que le sitúa entre los equipos con mayor carga de los grandes clubes europeos. En el recuento provisional, solo el Arsenal presenta un registro superior, con 2.463, mientras que Liverpool aparece con 1.893. La diferencia con el resto también resulta significativa: Bayern suma 1.841, PSG 1.774, Atlético 1.360 y Barcelona 1.084. La preocupación está especialmente relacionada con varios futbolistas que han tenido una presencia muy elevada con sus selecciones. Yan Diomande, Marc Cucurella y Arda Güler completaron los 180 minutos de sus dos compromisos, mientras que Jude Bellingham se quedó en 173 y Dean Huijsen alcanzó los 135. Son nombres importantes en los planes del Madrid y todos regresan después de haber tenido una participación considerable durante la ventana internacional. No todos, sin embargo, vuelven con la misma sensación. Para algunos futbolistas, el parón también ha supuesto una oportunidad para recuperar confianza, protagonismo y buenas sensaciones. Es el caso de Vinicius, que ha firmado cinco goles con Brasil, o de Endrick, que ha sumado un tanto y una asistencia. El brasileño necesitaba volver a sentirse importante y ha encontrado en la selección un escenario para reivindicarse. También han tenido motivos para regresar satisfechos Brahim Díaz, con dos asistencias en sus compromisos con Marruecos, y Dumfries, que ha repartido otras dos con Países Bajos. Carlos Espí y Thiago Pitarch, por su parte, han seguido acumulando experiencias con la Sub-21 española. Para ellos, el parón ha sido una oportunidad de crecimiento y de ganar confianza en un contexto diferente al del día a día en Valdebebas. El reto ahora pasa por equilibrar ambas realidades. Mourinho ha recuperado a todos sus futbolistas después de más de una semana de compromisos internacionales, viajes y esfuerzos repartidos por distintos continentes. Algunos regresan con muchos minutos en las piernas; otros, con la confianza reforzada. La gestión de ese desgaste será uno de los primeros asuntos que deberá resolver el Madrid en la vuelta a la competición.

articles.title: El Illes Balears Palma Futsal vende muy cara su hegemonía en la Copa Intercontinental (4-5)
articles.standfirst: El Sporting Clube gana su primera Copa Intercontinental e inscribe el nombre de Portugal en el palmarés de la competición
articles.summary: El Sporting Clube gana su primera Copa Intercontinental e inscribe el nombre de Portugal en el palmarés de la competición
articles.body: El Sporting Clube de Portugal levantó su primera Copa Intercontinental (en la primera final de esta competición a la que llegaba un equipo luso) acabando con la hegemonía de Illes Balears Palma Futsal en esta competición (4-5) tras una trayectoria inmaculada que le llevó a ganar en Foz do Iguaçú y dos veces en Palma de Mallorca. Y demostrando, pese a la derrota, lo gran campeón que ha sido durante todos estos años, dejando hasta el último suspiro en la pista. Sólo se habían jugado 68 segundos cuando Alex Merlim, en una conducción con la pierna derecha, sorprendió a Dennis Cavalcanti con un espectacular remate con la izquierda. No empezaban bien las cosas para los de Antonio Vadillo que, en un arranque de partido brusco, sólo veían cómo los árbitros no dejaban jugar, cayendo las faltas y las tarjetas para ambos equipos, sobre todo para los palmesanos. No se habían cumplido los nueve minutos y ya les habían señalado la quinta falta. En este escenario se encontró más cómodo el conjunto de Nuno Dias, que aprovechó las circunstancias para dejar casi sentenciado el encuentro antes del descanso con los goles de Chiskhala, Tomás Paçó y Diogo Santos en grandes acciones de los lisboetas. Lo intentó Illes Balears Palma Futsal desde el pitido inicial del segundo tiempo, pero volvió a ver cómo los árbitros cortaban con faltas muchas de sus acciones. Los de Antonio Vadillo, pero los de Nuno Dias, conscientes de que el reloj corría a su favor, trataban de que se jugara lo mínimo posible. Fabinho encontró el premio que tanto buscó Illes Balears Palma Futsal y dio nueve minutos y 44 segundos de esperanza a los de Palma. Instantes después un bocadillo entre Rocha y Bruno Pinto sobre el propio Fabinho provocó una fenomenal tangana que, tras ser revisada por los árbitros paraguayos quedó en nada, pero confirmó que la tensión en el Arena Cláudio Petrycovski era máxima. Tomás Pacó castigó una incorporación de Dennis Cavalcanti y el quinto subió al electrónico. Con más corazón que juego, Carlos Gómez estrellaba instantes después un balón en el palo. El reloj caminaba inexorablemente hacia el final del partido. Deivao conseguía un gol más en su cuenta y en la de Illes Balears Palma Futsal, que demostró que moriría hasta el final. Se tuvo que lucir Sukhov en sendos remates de Lucao y Deivao. Antonio Vadillo pidió tiempo muerto para hacer el último intento con Fabinho como portero jugador. Illes Balears prácticamente necesitaba un gol en cada posesión en el juego de cinco. Llegó el 3-5 de Ernesto y 1'49'' por jugarse. Carlos Gómez puso el 4-5 con 45 segundos por jugarse, y, lo que es más importante dando, al menos una opción más a su equipo. Recuperó el balón con 33 segundos y, ahora sí Nuno Dias pidió tiempo muerto. Dispuso de varios remates pero Sukhov no concedió ninguna e Illes Balears Palma pone punto y aparte en su historia en la Copa Intercontinental. Con Sporting Clube de Portugal como campeón e Illes Balears Palma Futsal, segundo; tercero fue el A Carlos Barbosa F, que se impuso al anfitrión, Pato Futsal, (4-2) y quinto el Bintang Timur Surabaya tras ganar (8-0) al Al-Ula de Arabia Saudí. FICHA TÉCNICA Arena Cláudio Petrycovski, 4.500 espectadores ILLES BALEARS PALMA: Dennis Cavalcanti; Deivao, Diego Nunes, Ernesto y Fabinho. También jugaron: Júlio Zanotto, Machado, Piqueras, Charuto, Carlos Gómez, Lucao, David Peña, Alisson Neves. SPORTING CLUBE PORTUGAL: Sukhov; Wesley, Erick Mendonça, Bruno y Alex Merlim. También jugaron: Diogo Santos, Tomás Paçó, Felipe Rufino, Bruno Pinto, Rocha, Chiskhala, Felipe Valerio y Rubén Teixeira. articles.title: Arsenal 0-2 Lyon: French side show Gunners bridge to gap
articles.summary: In a difficult defeat by French giants Lyon, Arsenal were shown the gap they need to bridge to challenge for the Champions League.
articles.body:
It is only 18 months since Arsenal tasted European glory, but they are not a team on many people's list of favourites for this season's Women's Champions League.

That is because not only have the Gunners disappointed across their opening 15 matches of the season, but also the elite teams in Europe seem to have gone up another level.

In the space of seven days, Arsenal have witnessed first hand what it takes to reach those heights - and the gap they must bridge.

Last week, they were resilient at Barcelona to earn a very respectable 1-1 draw, but were fortunate the Spanish side were not clinical with their chances at Camp Nou.

On Thursday night, they were outplayed at home in losing 2-0 to an excellent Lyon side , who look on course to match or better their runner-up finish from last season.

One point from such games could be pleasing - but that only shows the work Arsenal need to do to be considered one of the top teams in Europe.

French giants Lyon outclass Arsenal in Women's Champions League

Arsenal came into Thursday's defeat by Lyon off the back of a fifth successive Women's Super League draw at Emirates Stadium against London City Lionesses.

In contrast, Lyon have been flying domestically, winning all nine of their matches, scoring 49 goals, and then not conceding any in their unbeaten Champions League run.

Such form sets the pace and it was clear at Meadow Park that they were superior to Arsenal in every department.

Vibrant Germany international Jule Brand gave them the lead midway through the first half and Melchie Dumornay sealed the win with a powerful strike in the 57th minute.

Arsenal defender Leah Williamson said the "better team won the game" and manager Renee Slegers highlighted the difference in physicality between the teams.

"Compared to last year when we played Lyon [in the semi-finals], they are even better now. They have standout individual quality," Slegers said.

"They dominated in the first half. We had solutions for the second half and had more presence. We wore them down better but it still didn't lead to open chances."

Lyon had a 3.33 expected goals ratio on Thursday, serving up 23 shots to Arsenal's seven. They created six big chances and 14 of their shots were inside the box.

Dumornay oozed quality, midfielder Lily Yohannes showed composure and Brand was very impressive both defensively and going forward for Lyon, deployed in a new position.

Those individuals have benefitted from the expertise of former Barcelona manager Jonatan Giraldez, who joined in June 2025 - the month after Arsenal won the Champions League - and has now had the time he needed to impose his style.

As a result, Lyon have gone up another level and the gap between these two teams has widened by Arsenal's drop-off this season.

Slegers also said Arsenal had "prepared all we could" for the intensity that Lyon brought in London - but it still did not have an impact.

Asked how far off Lyon they currently are, Slegers said: "It's 2-0 today and they are better than us but it doesn't mean if we were to play them again soon, this season, that it would be the same game again.

"We saw moments where we did well and we know from the last couple of years we can hurt Lyon.

"But for today, their pace and physicality helped them get too much dominance in the game and that is one of their strengths. Then it became hard for us."

Williamson 'aware of where the gaps are'

Williamson said Arsenal "know what they need to do to be better" and that they are aware of "where the gaps are" to Europe's elite.

They are already 12 points off the pace in the Women's Super League title race and are unlikely to qualify automatically for the Champions League quarter-finals.

"The level rises year on year. Everybody cops goals - we have to try not to and we have to create," said Williamson following the defeat by Lyon.

"We're all focused and we're all together. That's the most comforting thing for me - but this has been a tough period."

It has not all been bad despite disappointing results - and context is important.

Over a gruelling seven days, they have faced European holders Barcelona, WSL high-flyers London City Lionesses and record Champions League winners Lyon.

They showed grit and resilience out in Barcelona last week - traits that have not been on show enough for Arsenal this season, but are clearly there.

Players like Williamson, striker Alessia Russo and summer signings Georgia Stanway and Ona Batlle know what it takes to compete at the highest level.

Arsenal invested in the summer transfer window and brought in proven, experienced players, but that has not translated into results - yet.

Giraldez said time with his players has helped improve Lyon and perhaps that is what Arsenal need - patience.

"I think they are changing now. They made a good game against Barcelona and it's very difficult to go there and get a point," said Giraldez.

"The game against London City was much better. It's not just about them, but also about us. Now we have improved and play better football than last year.

"I think it is a matter of time [for Arsenal]. They have a good coach and good players. In general, they have all the ingredients to have a good season."

articles.standfirst: Torneio reunirá 31 seleções e mais de 120 atletas com transmissão ao vivo pela internet.
articles.summary: Torneio reunirá 31 seleções e mais de 120 atletas com transmissão ao vivo pela internet.
articles.body:
A orla da Praia dos Cavaleiros será o ponto de encontro do esporte praiano nos dias 5 e 6 de dezembro, quando acontece a 9ª edição do Super Mundialito de Altinha 2026. A competição reunirá 31 seleções e cerca de 120 competidores nas categorias Open A e Open B, consolidando a cidade de Macaé como polo regional e nacional de modalidades esportivas ao ar livre.

O torneio marca o encerramento do calendário da Liga Nacional Em Alta e terá peso especial na reta final da temporada, distribuindo pontuação multiplicada por 1,5 no ranking geral. Com a presença garantida de referências da altinha de diversas regiões, a disputa promete alto nível técnico pelas primeiras colocações e troféus.

articles.standfirst: España conoce mañana en Nyon su rival en los cuartos de la Nations: Alemania, Francia o Portugal
articles.summary: España conoce mañana en Nyon su rival en los cuartos de la Nations: Alemania, Francia o Portugal
articles.body: España conocerá hoy su rival de los cuartos de la Nations League en el sorteo que se celebra en Nyon (Suiza), a partir de las 12:00 horas, por un puesto en la fase final. La selección quedó finalmente segunda de su liguilla tras la derrota en el Metropolitano y tendrá que afrontar un rival del bombo 1, de los tres que acabaron primeras de grupo salvo el equipo de Tuchel al coincidir en el mismo grupo de La Roja. Y lo cierto es que no se puede hablar de preferencias o de rival a evitar. Salga la bola que salga, el cruce promete. Portugal, Francia o Alemania, un tridente de potencias del Viejo Continente. España paga también el precio de quedar segundo jugando el segundo partido lejos de casa. La ida de los cuartos se disputan en Mestalla entre el 25 y el 27 de marzo y la vuelta casi acto seguido entre el 28 y el 30 del mismo mes. Los cuatro ganadores jugaran una final four entre el 9 y el 13 de junio en una sede aún por confirmar. España sabe que no será fácil. Los tres rivales han amargado alguna vez o más la fiesta a La Roja, pero lo cierto es que los precedentes más recientes son más que positivos. Francia y Alemania llegan con aires renovados con mucho peso en el banquillo: Zidane y Klopp. En el caso de Les Bleus, la presión sin duda es más para ellos, que han visto como la Roja se ha convertido en su bestia negra. Parecían imbatibles hasta que llegó Luis de la Fuente, sin ir más lejos en la semifinal del Mundial. Pero es que además España se impuso también en la Nations de 2025 y 2024. Sin embargo, la Francia de Mbappé y Olise se puede agarrar a la final de la Nations de 2021 con triunfo gracias al polémico gol de Kylian en fuera de juego. Alemania es la incógnita. No deja de ser Alemania, pero busca recuperar su gen ganador de la mano de Klopp y más tras el fiasco del Mundial. El último cruce no decepcionó con un triunfo de España en los cuartos de la Eurocopa en Berlín y que aún le cuesta pitos a Cucurella cuando juega en Alemania por aquella famosa mano. En la anterior etapa dorada de España, con Luis Aragonés y Del Bosque, los germanos también mordieron el polvo en la final de la Euro de 2008 o en las semifinales del Mundial de 2010. No conviene fiarse porque Alemania sigue siendo la selección con mejor palmarés en Europa, con cuatro Mundiales y tres Eurocopas, aunque España, gracias a su esplendor desde 2008, ya se ha puesto segunda. Y luego queda Portugal, otra selección que ha sufrido mucho con España y también en este Mundial, el último de Cristiano. Nuevo duelo ya sin la leyenda, que ha anunciado recientemente su despedida. Está muy reciente su derrota en los octavos del Mundial, que dolió casi más que la derrota en la final de la Nations de 2025. articles.title: BBC cuts: Next round of savings will be more noticeable to audiences, report warns
articles.summary: The BBC has already cut jobs, programmes and services but has further to go to reach its £500m target.
articles.body:
Further job losses and programme cuts at the BBC will be more noticeable to audiences than previous savings measures, a new report has warned.

The corporation announced plans earlier this year to cut about 1,800 roles and close some programmes and services, but it has further savings to make to reach its £500m target.

In its report, the National Audit Office (NAO) anticipated the BBC's next round of cost-cutting measures will be more difficult to deliver and more perceptible to audiences.

The BBC welcomed the report and said it has "consistently argued that the current funding model is not sustainable and needs reform".

The NAO's report also said the BBC's current measures are expected to reduce the BBC's workforce by 11% over three years.

Gareth Davies, head of the NAO, said: "As the BBC approaches charter renewal in just over a year's time, there is no doubt that there are difficult choices ahead."

The BBC's finances have declined in recent years as a result of falling licence fee income and rising production costs.

The organisation has so far achieved savings by reducing staffing levels, rationalising its estate, modernising technology, simplifying processes and changing the mix and scope of content and services, the public spending watchdog said.

The NAO found the BBC's licence fee income fell by 26% in real terms over the last decade, due in part to the significant changes in audience habits.

The proportion of UK adults using BBC television, iPlayer, radio or online services on an average week also fell from 90% in 2021-22 to 81% in 2025-26, the NAO said.

The report noted the corporation's public service broadcasting operating defecit reached £209m in the last financial year.

The BBC has already announced plans to reduce spending by about 10%, including cuts to programming across its news, nations and content divisions.

Celebrity Mastermind, Blankety Blank, Live At The Apollo, Football Focus, Ski Sunday and RuPaul's Drag Race UK are among the TV programmes to have been cut so far.

Radio programmes are also being dropped from the schedules, such as You and Yours and The World Tonight on BBC Radio 4.

The corporation has also announced plans to close the linear broadcast services of BBC Radio 4 Extra, BBC Three and BBC Scotland, with the latter two becoming online-only services.

The NAO said the BBC expects to face difficult choices about the scale and scope of its services as part of its latest savings programme, with further content reductions expected to have a greater impact on audiences.

It warned the corporation was likely to find it harder to identify further savings following its previous cost-cutting programmes.

The NAO also found the broadcaster had not properly monitored the cumulative impact of its previous savings on audiences, service quality and organisational capability.

It also raised concerns about the BBC's risk management and governance arrangements, and said stronger oversight would be needed to deliver the more demanding savings programme.

In response to the report, the BBC said it welcomed the findings, and added that it has had to "make tough decisions due to sustained financial pressures driven by declining licence fee income, changing audience behaviour, increased competition and rising costs".

Berangere Michel, the BBC's group chief financial officer, said: "We welcome this report and are pleased that the NAO has acknowledged the significant savings already delivered by the BBC, with the programme on track to meet its target one year ahead of schedule.

"The BBC must respond to significant cost pressures while reinventing for a changing world. This continues to require tough decisions, while ensuring that the impacts on audiences and colleagues are minimised.

"We accept the NAO's recommendations and have already begun implementing them to strengthen the delivery of our current savings programme, while recognising there are further opportunities to build on this progress.

She added: "We will continue to engage with government to secure a new Charter that provides sufficient, sustainable and universal funding so the BBC can deliver for audiences for generations to come."

articles.title: New CFB Rumors Reveal SEC NIL Agreements 'Causing an Uproar' Among Agents
articles.summary: Some agents representing student-athletes are unhappy with how the SEC is standardizing NIL and revenue sharing contracts, ESPN's Max Olson reported Thursday.
articles.body:
Some agents representing student-athletes are unhappy with how the SEC is standardizing NIL and revenue sharing contracts, ESPN's Max Olson reported Thursday.

Olson reported there is "an uproar among agents concerned that the conference has loaded the contracts with terms they consider unfair to student-athletes."

SEC presidents voted in October to follow in the Big Ten's footsteps by approving a standardized NIL and revenue sharing contract framework, On3's Pete Nakos .

Olson reported multiple agents told ESPN the SEC's standardized contracts are "way worse" than the Big Ten's.

"The standardized contract is being met with serious pushback from players' agents, and sources told ESPN that several top agencies have informed schools that their clients will not sign the SEC contract with the current language," Olson reported.

Olson added several agents and general managers "told ESPN they wonder whether the SEC contract could become a disadvantage for league members competing for top transfers."

247Sports' Chris Hummer reported the SEC's standardized contract "could be a chill on multi-year deals."

"Agents say players who expect to outperform their contracts have little incentive to sign long-term when schools have no obligation to renegotiate," Hummer reported. "247Sports has already heard of several notable extensions on hold."

According to Olson, the standard contract structure gives the SEC power to terminate deals for a variety of reasons while requiring players to pay back 50 percent of their remaining money as liquidated damages in order to transfer or launch a professional career.

Athletes would have to pay their buyout in full before they could transfer from an SEC school, Olson reported.

Programs also wouldn't be required to enter players into the transfer portal "until after the final game of the final year of the agreement," according to Olson. Current NCAA rules state DI schools generally must enter student-athlete's names into the portal within two days of the player's written request.

According to Hummer, programs have been told to seek SEC approval in order to make any adjustments to these contracts.

The new details regarding the contract standardization comes after Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger reported last week the SEC had proposed a de facto salary cap and luxury tax system that took into account both revenue sharing and some NIL deals.

The news followed the Big Ten's announcement of its own NIL spending cap. It also comes ahead of what is anticipated to be a December U.S. House of Representatives vote on the Protect College Sports Act, a bill seeking to regulate NIL and revenue sharing that passed the U.S. Senate in September.

These changes come amid ongoing high school recruiting as well as contract negotiations with returning players.

One notable SEC player reportedly already working out a new contract is Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor, who On3's Chris Low and Pete Nakos reported last week was finalizing a $7.5 million deal worth up to $9 million with incentives. Olson reported Thursday that Taylor is still in the negotiating process.

The SEC has less than two months before the 10-day transfer window opens Jan. 4.

articles.title: Indiana's Curt Cignetti calls report listing him as candidate for potential Michigan opening 'fake news'
articles.summary: The outspoken Cignetti continues to make his voice heard online, this time in response to his name being mentioned in college football's latest coaching cycl...
articles.body:
Before orchestrating one of the greatest turnarounds in sports, Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti famously uttered the line , "It's pretty simple, I win — Google me."

More than two years later, and after his Hoosiers won the program's first national championship , people apparently need to do something else: Check his X account.

Because, at this point, Cignetti is posting regularly with reckless abandon. On Thursday night, with his name surprisingly being mentioned in the latest coaching cycle, Cignetti fired off his latest eye-catching social media post .

With Indiana in position for a third straight College Football Playoff bid, he called out a CBS Sports report listing him as a candidate for a potential Michigan opening as "fake news," which Cignetti claimed was "created by three SEC media writers."

"Nice try," he added in the post on X, along with a clown emoji.

Cignetti has been taking shots at the SEC for a while now . Earlier this month, following the season's first College Football Playoff rankings , in which the SEC had four more teams than the Big Ten, he noted on his weekly radio show that "the SEC gets a lot of love from ESPN." While ESPN doesn't have say on the CFP rankings, the CFP has a TV contract with ESPN, which is the exclusive rights holder of SEC football.

The report Cignetti responded to on Thursday, however, came from CBS Sports. CBS is actually among the networks that are part of the Big Ten's media rights agreement.

Regardless, Cignetti labeling the report as "fake news" is the most significant part of his post, considering it appears to indicate he'll be sticking around Bloomington after this season. Besides, the hypothetical candidacy CBS Sports outlined involves Michigan parting ways with head coach Kyle Whittingham. It's yet to be seen if that will actually happen this year.

CBS Sports cited its sources when reporting Cignetti has expressed concerns about funding at Indiana as well as the Hoosiers' "ability to sustain winning at this level."

Indiana is 36-3 with Cignetti at the helm. He's on the verge of leading the Hoosiers to a third straight 10-plus-win season. Before he arrived, they didn't have a single one in program history.

Indiana inked Cignetti to another contract extension back in February. It reportedly goes through the 2033 season and averages more than $13 million per season.

Cignetti posted on X twice in September, both for advertisements. He didn't post at all in October. This month, he's already posted five times.

He conveyed his disappointment in the CFP committee after the Hoosiers plummeted five spots in the rankings despite being off for the week . Then he defended USC head coach Lincoln Riley in the aftermath of Indiana effectively dashing the Trojans' CFP hopes.

Since taking the Hoosiers job, he's never minced words at the mic. During his news conference this week, he monologued about the constant critique of Indiana's schedule .

Toward the end of those remarks, Cignetti said he thinks that hypercritical dialogue about the Hoosiers helps motivate them.

"And that's why I'm not afraid to keep it alive," he said. "And you know what? I'm 65 years old, and I really don't give a s***."

articles.title: Rose Lavelle named to 2026 NWSL Best XI
articles.summary: Rose Lavelle helped Gotham FC wins its first NWSL Shield, given to the league’s regular season champion, with a club-record 61 points (18-5-7)
articles.body:
Four Gotham FC players have been named to the 2026 NWSL Best XI First and Second Teams, presented by Amazon Prime. That includes Mount Notre Dame graduate Rose Lavelle.

Goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger, defender Tierna Davidson and midfielder Jaelin Howell earned First Team honors, while Lavelle was named to the Second Team .

The four selections recognize key contributors to a Gotham FC squad that captured its first NWSL Shield, given to the league's regular season champion, with a club-record 61 points and an 18-5-7 record. The club also boasted the league's best defensive record, conceding just 23 goals in 30 matches. Gotham lost in the playoff semifinals Nov. 15 to Kansas City, who has 2015 Oak Hills graduate Bayley Feist on its roster. Feist has been in the NWSL since 2019 and has started 10 matches for Kansas City this season. They will play Washington Spirit for the league title 8 p.m. Nov. 21.

Lavelle, the Mount Notre Dame grad , earned Second Team recognition after another impactful season directing Gotham FC's attack. The U.S. international recorded four goals and three assists in 25 appearances, including 22 starts, while ranking eighth in the NWSL with 36 completed dribbles. The reigning NWSL Championship MVP logged 1,892 minutes during the regular season.

In September, Lavelle signed a contract extension with Gotham through the 2029 NWSL season. She played a defining role in Gotham FC's historic 2025 campaign, helping the club capture the NWSL Championship with the winning goal late in the final while earning NWSL Championship MVP honors. Gotham will play in a new stadium in Queens starting with the 2028 season.

Lavelle was just named to the 23-player U.S. Women's National Team roster for the 2026 Concacaf W Championship, where the United States will compete for a berth in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil.

The United States will open the tournament against El Salvador on Nov. 27 in Mansfield, Texas, with a victory securing qualification for the 2027 World Cup. The tournament will also determine qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
