articles.title: Thursday Night Football: C.J. Stroud, Texans lead Colts 17-3 at halftime
articles.summary: Stroud threw two touchdown passes in the first half.
articles.body:
The Texans are doing what they need to do. Now, can they finish?

Four days after blowing a 17-0 lead over the Browns, Houston leads Indianapolis 17-3 at halftime.

The Texans outgained the Colts 202 to 125 in the first half but settled for Ka'imi Fairbairn's 27-yard field goal after stalling at the Indianapolis 9 in the closing seconds.

C.J. Stroud went 13-of-18 for 134 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. He now ranks third in team history in passing yards, surpassing David Carr (13,391).

He has 21 touchdown passes, two short of his career high for a season.

Stroud's touchdowns covered 42 yards to Nico Collins and 24 yards to Kayshon Boutte.

David Montgomery, who missed the previous four games with a groin injury, has 11 carries for 54 yards. Collins has two catches for 48 yards and a touchdown.

The Colts had four plays of over 20 yards, but went 0-for-1 in the red zone, missed two field goals and threw an interception.

The Colts scored their only points on Spencer Shrader's 34-yard field goal. But he missed from 56 and had a 62-yarder blocked by Logan Hall with 2:41 remaining in the half.

Daniel Jones was only 1-for-5 for 22 yards with an interception in the second quarter. He finished the half 7-of-17 for 109 yards and an interception.

Jonathan Taylor has eight carries for 17 yards.

Texans offensive tackle Trent Brown was questionable to return with a back injury. He had been alternating with Braden Smith at right tackle, but Smith played most of the half. Brown, though, did return before the half ended.

Texans defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins is questionable with an ankle injury.

articles.title: Thursday’s LSU vs. Tennessee injury report: Weeks officially out
articles.summary: Along with confirmation that Whit Weeks, we got surprising news for the Tigers
articles.body:
The second injury report is out for LSU vs. Tennessee and it's a busy one for both teams.

After being listed as questionable every day leading in to their game against Texas, then doubtful on the initial injury report yesterday, Whit Weeks is now listed as out.

It's been an incredibly unfortunate career for Weeks, as this could mark the 3rd straight season that ends with an injury. He has not played since breaking his fibula against Texas A&M in week 4.

The other notable news for LSU is wide receivers Jackson Harris and Winnie Watkins being listed as questionable. We've seen Harris come up hobbled a few times over the past few games, but he's shown grit and toughness and returns to the field. It is unclear what his specific injury is.

As for Watkins, he's been dealing with a torn ligament in his thumb since week 5 against McNeese, but has been playing through it.

Jhase Thomas remains probable, meaning he was likely limited in practice so far this week.

The new addition for LSU is Aidan Anding. This is the first time that we've seen him at all in 2026 after he tore his achilles in the spring scrimmage. Listed as probable, it appears that the sophomore will make his season debut in Knoxville on Saturday.

As for Tennessee, they have 10 players listed as out. The big news, though, is that quarterback George MacIntyre is not listed. He left their game last weekend against Texas A&M in the 3rd quarter with a knee injury and did not return. After taking over for Faizon Brandon as the Volunteers starting QB, MacIntyre is 4-1 and has helped them reach the top-10 in the College Football Playoff rankings.

Tennessee comes in to Saturday's contest ranked #9 and 8-2, while LSU fell out of the rankings following last week's last second loss to Texas that dropped them to 6-4.

Kickoff is for 2:30 pm central in Neyland Stadium on Saturday and will be telecasted on ABC.

articles.title: Premier League Clubs Target Ronaldo Successor Carlos Forbs
articles.summary: Premier League giants are circling Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs after he took over the Portugal No. 7 shirt. Here is the latest transfer news and fee deta...
articles.body:
Carlos Forbs is no longer just a young winger. He is now the man wearing the Portugal No. 7 shirt. That is the number Cristiano Ronaldo wore for years before he retired from international football, according to ESPN . Forbs took over the jersey after a strong showing against Wales earlier this week. Now, a host of Premier League clubs are watching his every move. TEAMtalk reports that teams like Aston Villa, Newcastle United, and Brighton & Hove Albion are tracking the situation closely. Everton and Brentford are also looking to make a deal before the price goes up. The 22-year-old's value is rising fast, and the window to buy might be closing.

Manchester United is not waiting around either. The Red Devils are looking to fix their defense with new faces. The club is evaluating Jarrad Branthwaite of Everton and Calvin Bassey of Fulham, per reports. They are also monitoring Fulham left back Antonee Robinson. Robinson worked with Mauricio Pochettino while playing for the USMNT. United could also revisit interest in Barcelona's Alejandro Balde. The club knows it needs to act fast to build a team that can win.

Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie says he does not want to leave his club, but that does not stop the rumors. Gazzetta dello Sport indicates that Pochettino still desires to bring the 28-year-old USMNT international back to Old Trafford. Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg is a target for Juve. Securing the 31-year-old may hinge on McKennie's situation. A €40 million bid might be required by United to secure his signature. That is a lot of cash to spend on a midfielder who says he wants to stay put.

Barcelona is also in the market for a center back. Mundo Deportivo reports they are looking at Internazionale's Alessandro Bastoni and Borussia Dortmund's Nico Schlotterbeck. They are also eyeing Manchester United's Lisandro Martínez. Although the Blaugrana agreed with Bastoni last summer, manager Hansi Flick caused the deal to collapse by focusing on other priorities. The 27-year-old remains open to a move. The club has also renewed efforts to sign Brighton's Luka Vuskovic. Vuskovic, 19, arrived at the Seagulls this summer from Spurs for £46 million. Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, and Liverpool are also watching his situation.

Bruno Fernandes is at the center of a contract standoff. AC Milan and Galatasaray have shown interest in signing the Manchester United attacking midfielder as a free agent in July, per reports. Old Trafford remains the destination for the 32-year-old via a new contract extension from United until 2029. No deal exists between the two parties at present. Last June, Fernandes rejected a substantial proposal from Saudi Arabian side Al Hilal.

Real Madrid is keeping a close eye on Brighton & Hove Albion midfielder Andres Chema. They are considering him as they look to strengthen their squad.

articles.title: Chiefs Had Inside Connection in Josh Downs Trade With Colts
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs pulled the trigger on trading for a wide receiver ahead of the NFL trade deadline. They acquired Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colt...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs pulled the trigger on trading for a wide receiver ahead of the NFL trade deadline.

They acquired Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts, and instantly plugged him into the offense in Week 10 against the Atlanta Falcons. He made a great first impression, catching five passes for 53 yards and a touchdown.

Kansas City Chiefs Consulted With Chris Ballard Before Trading for WR Josh Downs

Ballard spent four years with the Chiefs from 2013-2016. He began with the team as the Director of Player Personnel, then was promoted to Director of Football Operations. In 2017 in left Kansas Cit to become the Colts general manager.

Unfortunately for Ballard, he was fired by Indianapolis this past October after 10 years. While speaking to the media on Thursday, Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy said he talked to Ballard about Downs, and was sold on him afterward.

"I had a personal friend of mine, Chris Ballard, and he raved about him, Bieniemy said of Downs. "I've head a number of people talk about him in the past. He's an outstanding individual. He's an intelligent kid. He works his tail off. It's important to him. When you combine all that with his God-given ability, you're very excited about what you have. I thought the receiver group did a great job of embracing and helping him along. He did a great job, he stepped up and made a few plays. He's ready to continue to move forward and getting to know the playbook as much as he can."

Josh Downs Is Giving Chiefs WR Corps a Shot in the Arm

Not only did Downs produce in his Chiefs debut , he opened things up for other receivers. Rookies Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong each caught the first touchdown passes of their careers against the Falcons. Rashee Rice had a stellar day with five receptions for 82 yards.

Downs is a top tier route runner, and excels at getting open against man coverage — something Kansas City's offense has desperately needed over the past few years. If Downs can continue to be a go-to target for quarterback Patrick Mahomes , and take attention away from other Chiefs WRs, the passing attack will be much improved during the second half of the season.

articles.title: Fox teams with Univision for World Cup bid; NBC bows out
articles.summary: The true contenders for the 2030 FIFA World Cup auction are becoming clear. Fox, the incumbent English-language World Cup partner, has reportedly submitted a...
articles.body:
The true contenders for the 2030 FIFA World Cup auction are becoming clear.

Fox, the incumbent English-language World Cup partner, has reportedly submitted a joint bid with Univision, the Spanish-language broadcaster owned by TelevisaUnivision, according to John Ourand of Puck . Additionally, NBC, the incumbent Spanish-language partner which was previously reported to be taking its decision on whether or not to bid down to the wire, has opted not to submit an offer for World Cup rights. The other two corporate owners of big-four broadcast networks — Disney and Skydance — were previously reported to have decided against bidding, leaving the Fox-Univision team-up as the only offer not from a streaming service.

The joint bid effectively means Fox and Univision will try to maintain the status quo by keeping the World Cup entirely on broadcast television, with the only difference being Univision stepping in for Telemundo. The remaining companies that have reportedly submitted bids consist only of streamers: Netflix, YouTube, and Amazon. Apple was previously reported to have decided against a bid. DAZN was reported earlier this week as a likely bidder, though it is still unclear if the streamer submitted a bid.

Fox and Univision opting to pair their bids together solves for FIFA's desire to bundle both English- and Spanish-language rights into a single package. A Fox-only offer would've likely required at least some Spanish-language matches to be broadcast on the sparsely distributed Fox Deportes cable network. Univision offers the power of a widely distributed and free-to-air broadcast network.

It's important to note, the possibility of World Cup games airing on broadcast television would remain open even if FIFA awarded rights to a streamer. FIFA's recent World Cup media rights deal with Netflix in Spain, for instance, includes carve outs for a certain number of games to be shown on free-to-air broadcast. Spain, however, has government regulations mandating such provisions, while no such provisions exist in the United States.

Importantly, Ourand reports that most companies that submitted bids did so only for the 2030 World Cup. FIFA had reportedly encouraged offers that included both the 2030 and 2034 tournaments, but it seems that the unfavorable time zones for the American audience played a role in the decision to limit bids to 2030, which is set to be hosted by Spain, Portugal, and Morocco. The 2034 tournament is slated for Saudi Arabia, which is eight hours ahead of the Eastern time zone and also faces the possibility of a shift from summer to winter, similar to the 2022 tournament in Qatar.

Earlier this week, Netflix was classified as the "frontrunner" to win rights , according to a report in The Guardian . Netflix has seemed to be a favored partner for FIFA recently, with the tournament organizer having already awarded Netflix the aforementioned Spain deal, and also having awarded the streamer U.S. broadcast rights for the 2027 Women's World Cup several years ago.

FIFA is expected to decide on a winner for 2030 by the end of this year.

articles.title: What is it like to miss a season through injury?
articles.summary: Not pleasant to be around and staring at a wall for hours after being told you are not going to the World Cup - what's it like for footballers when they miss a season due to serious injury?
articles.body:
"I told my mother. I sat with her and I told her: 'Listen, I don't think I can play any more'," says Dejan Kulusevski in a moving interview about his injury nightmare.

It is 18 months since Tottenham and Sweden winger Kulusevski, 26, last started a competitive match.

Spurs have won the Europa League, sacked both Ange Postecoglou and Thomas Frank, "mutually agreed" to part ways with Igor Tudor and appointed Roberto de Zerbi since the former Juventus player last started a first-team game for his club.

A serious knee injury two weeks from the end of the 2024-25 season forced him to miss the whole of the following campaign, as well as the 2026 World Cup.

"You feel like the whole world has forgotten about you," adds Kulusevski in an interview with Tottenham's in-house media , external about the emotional toll of being out for so long.

Thankfully, the player nicknamed 'Deki' has made a full recovery and is closing in on his first Tottenham start since 11 May 2025.

He is not the only footballer to question their career after having their world turned upside down by injury.

In the women's game, Everton club captain Megan Finnigan recently returned from a cruciate ligament injury after 602 days out. , external

"The amount of times the thought of retirement entered my head during rehab was a lot," Finnigan, 28, tells BBC Sport.

Countless hours in the gym away from team-mates, boredom, setbacks and frustration - what is it like for a player at the peak of their game to miss a season because of injury?

'I am a different man now' - Kulusevski on return after 526 days

Kulusevski out for a 'few months' - Postecoglou

Before Crystal Palace visited Tottenham a fortnight from the end of the 2024-25 campaign, Kulusevski had much to look forward to.

Off the pitch, he was making plans to marry his partner Eldina Ahmic, a former midfielder with Swedish club Brommapojkarna and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

On the pitch, there was a Europa League final against Manchester United coming up.

Everything changed in that match against Palace.

In the early stages, Kulusevski stayed down after a challenge with Marc Guehi. He was able to climb to his feet and walk unaided off the pitch and straight down the tunnel.

But in that moment, his problems were only just starting.

"It was pain, but it didn't hurt that much," Kulusevski says, recalling the patella and cartilage injury in his right knee.

"I could feel that the knee was moving a little bit too much."

The initial diagnosis from Tottenham was that the £25m signing from Juventus, who arrived in the summer of 2023, would be out for "at least a few months".

Due to complications, those months turned into a year and Kulusevski's dream career threatened to turn into a nightmare.

He travelled to Bilbao on crutches to watch his team-mates beat United in the Europa League final.

"That was one of the hardest days of my life," he says. "It was so beautiful to see all the people happy, but for me I was going there with crutches, I couldn't work.

"I couldn't even go and get my medal because it was too slippy to go on that thing [platform].

"Seeing the team celebrating on the bus [outside Tottenham Hotspur Stadium] was probably one of the most difficult parts of this journey because you feel so alone.

"You feel like the whole world has forgot about you and what you put in."

As months went by, Kulusevski underwent multiple operations and was even offered a knee transplant as a treatment option, which he rejected.

"You get stressed because nothing works," he says.

Then came another crushing blow delivered in a phone call with Sweden boss Graham Potter. Stockholm-born Kulusevski, who had played for his country since the age of 19, would not be going to the 2026 World Cup.

He had hoped to recover in time to be selected.

"I just stared at the wall for three hours because I really believed I would do it," he says.

It is not just the players who suffer when they are out for so long; the people around them feel the emotional toll as well.

"Seeing him miss the Europa League final and the World Cup, every Premier League game last season, seeing him skipping around on his crutches, those parts were really difficult," Eldina, Kulusevski's wife, says.

As recently as this past summer, Kulusevski wondered whether he would play again.

"It had been one year and two months and I could still not walk up the stairs like a normal guy.

"I wasn't going to give up, but I also had to think if this didn't work out, what am I going to do, because I am 26 and I have to have some sort of plan."

Enormous comfort came from Leonie, Kulusevski's two-year-old daughter, during his bleakest days.

"I said if I cannot play football any more, I will still have fun with her."

Then, after multiple setbacks, came a crucial breakthrough.

His knee had healed sufficiently for specialists to give him permission to train again.

On 19 October, Kulusevski was given a hero's reception by Spurs fans when he made his first appearance in 526 days.

It came in Tottenham 's 3-1 win over Coventry City as an 87th-minute substitute.

Waiting for him after the final whistle were Eldina and Leonie, his daughter wearing a Spurs shirt with the number 526 on the back, along with the words 'My Hero'.

He made his Sweden return this month, coming off the bench in a win against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

"Every day is just beautiful now," says Kulusevski, who has made four substitute appearances totalling 42 minutes for his club this season.

Research suggests female footballers are two to six times more likely to suffer anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries than their male counterparts.

Everton captain Finnigan remembers how she "completely lost my sparkle" as she endured the long road to recovery.

"It's not comfortable to think back how I was," Finnigan tells BBC Radio Merseyside's Giulia Bould.

"Anyone that knows me knows I'm very bubbly, quite loud, I like to be at the centre of things. I completely lost myself in rehab, completely lost my sparkle as my mum says.

"How I was in this building is not nice to think back on. I was always thinking what other people were thinking about me. I was not pleasant to be around as I was struggling so much.

"I was also thinking 'no-one wants to be around me'. I was just miserable. Everyone in this building has seen me cry over the past 18 months."

Listen: Megan Finnigan 'Really special feeling to be back'

Finnigan - Everton 's longest-serving women's player having joined the Blues at the age of nine - suffered her injury in an FA Cup tie against Tottenham in January 2025. She did not return to competitive action until September of this year.

"I was in quite a difficult place mentally," she adds.

One thing that helped her through her lowest moments was writing down her feelings.

"It was an absolute whirlwind of a rehab, a rollercoaster," she adds.

"Anyone who went through it with me will tell you that. I am really glad I kept a diary as proof I did it and survived it."

Former Arsenal and England midfielder Fara Williams points to how some players who suffer serious injuries in the Women's Super League face specific worries.

"While they are going through rehab, there are financial worries, bills to pay; they are on short contracts so you don't have that stability," says Williams.

"While you are managing the injury, mentally you are stressing, wondering where the next contract is coming from. When you are stressed, I imagine that doesn't help with the healing of the injury."

Micah Richards suffered multiple long-term knee and hamstring injuries before he retired in 2019 while at Aston Villa .

A few months later the former Manchester City and England defender opened up to BBC Sport about injuries and the "dark side of football".

"I was in a lonely place for a long time, and I did not know how to get out of it," he said at the time.

"Deep down, I probably knew it was already over, but for most of the two and a half years between my 295th and final game as a professional, against Wolves in October 2016, and the day I announced my retirement in July 2019, I was living in denial.

"I could run and I could jump - but I couldn't twist on my right knee, and it would not get any better. Whatever I tried, it did not make any difference.

"There were times while I was injured at Villa when I felt like I was a ghost.

"They told me to come in three times a week, then two. Then one.

"I would go into the gym and tell myself 'I am all right, I am all right, I am all right' but actually I had no idea how to deal with what was happening to me, and my body."

articles.title: Cazada a Mbeumo: la primera estrella del deporte víctima de la epidemia del GTA 6
articles.standfirst: Bryan Mbeumo (Manchester United) fue cazado jugando al GTA 6 de madrugada antes de acudir a su primer entrenamiento con Mauricio Pochettino
articles.summary: Bryan Mbeumo (Manchester United) fue cazado jugando al GTA 6 de madrugada antes de acudir a su primer entrenamiento con Mauricio Pochettino
articles.body: El mundo lleva 13 años esperando el lanzamiento del famoso videojuego GTA 6, y las estrellas del deporte no son inmunes al atractivo y al carácter adictivo de este juego que amenaza con paralizar las oficinas (se prevé que sea el día con más ausencias laborales de todo el año). Alexander Isak, delantero del Liverpool, reconoció que "sí, creo que va a ser difícil localizarme a partir del día 19, cuando salga el GTA 6. Estaré totalmente encerrado en casa. Ese es el plan". Conor McGregor, leyenda de la UFC, anunció que daría el día libre a 400 empleados de sus diversos negocios para que pudieran jugar al GTA 6. Thibaut Courtois, portero del Real Madrid, compartió una imagen suya jugando pilotando un helicóptero en el GTA 6. Diversos estudios sostienen que el rendimiento de los deportistas podría "desplomarse" durante semanas tras el lanzamiento del GTA 6. "Prestad atención a lo que pase en noviembre, al rendimiento en la liga, en todas las ligas... sale el GTA 6. Fijaos en la NFL, fijaos en todas las ligas y veréis cómo cae el rendimiento, amigo. Durante el mes de noviembre, el rendimiento va a bajar", advirtió Steven Adams, pívot de los Houston Rockets en la NBA. Bryan Mbeumo, futbolista por el que el Manchester United pagó 82 millones de euros en 2025, expresó su entusiasmo con el lanzamiento del GTA 6. El delantero francocamerunés de 27 años no pudo resistirse a una partido nocturna y se quedó despierto hasta tarde para jugar al GTA6, cuando por la mañana Mauricio Pochettino, su nuevo entrenador en el United, comenzaba a trabajar. Bryan Mbeumo compartió en sus 'stories' de Instagram la pantalla de carga del juego de Rockstar junto a la palabra "histórico", justo cuando el reloj marcaba el inicio del jueves. "Ahora solo toca esperar; el juego hará que me quede en casa todos los días... después de entrenar", confesó Mbeumo antes del lanzamiento del GTA 6. Nick Littlehales, un reconocido experto en sueño para deportistas de élite, explica en 'Ozoon' los efectos que puede tener jugar a videojuegos hasta altas horas de la noche: "Te absorbe por completo; es una distracción muy atrayente que satisface el espíritu competitivo. Pero, al igual que ocurre cuando navegamos sin rumbo por YouTube o las redes sociales, es necesario establecer filtros y bloqueos propios. De lo contrario, puedes acabar haciendo algo realmente absurdo: jugar durante horas y horas, lo que terminará perjudicando tu rendimiento", declaró a Ozoon. "Sabemos que no es realista esperar que un jugador deje de jugar exactamente a las dos horas cuando está totalmente metido en la partida. Hay que aceptarlo y plantearles la cuestión: '¿Estás dispuesto a sacrificar tus horas de sueño nocturno para mantenerte despierto y estimulado? ¿Merece la pena?'. Si insisten, intentamos planificarlo; por ejemplo, permitiendo que jueguen hasta tarde los martes o los jueves... Es mejor mantener este tipo de conversaciones abiertas en lugar de prohibir tajantemente jugar por la noche. Si simplemente les impones normas estrictas, al final terminan recurriendo a pastillas para dormir o a suplementos no regulados que ni siquiera conocen, solo para poder aguantar el ritmo", acalar en declaraciones que reproduce el 'Daily Mail'. Declan Rice, estrella del Arsenal, reconoce en 'GQ' que "nunca puedo dormir después de los partidos nocturnos. Es imposible; me quedo demasiado alterado. Juego a Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto, FIFA... a cualquier cosa. Juego con un grupo de amigos. Es la adrenalina, todo eso... simplemente no logras calmarte".

articles.title: Pepe Brasín alerta del problema con Vinicius: "No puedes tener a una estrella con rol secundario"
articles.standfirst: El periodista analiza en 'Las Brasas de Pepe Brasín' de 'La Tribu' de Radio MARCA el regreso del brasileño al Real Madrid y las dificultades para encajar a todas las estrellas en un equipo que ha ganado sus últimos ocho partidos
articles.summary: El periodista analiza en 'Las Brasas de Pepe Brasín' de 'La Tribu' de Radio MARCA el regreso del brasileño al Real Madrid y las dificultades para encajar a todas las estrellas en un equipo que ha ganado sus últimos ocho partidos
articles.body: El regreso de Vinicius al Real Madrid plantea uno de los grandes dilemas de José Mourinho. El brasileño vuelve después de recuperar sensaciones con su selección, pero se encuentra con un equipo que ha encadenado ocho victorias consecutivas y que ha ofrecido su mejor versión sin él como protagonista. Una situación que Pepe Brasín ha analizado en su sección Las Brasas de La Tribu, en Radio MARCA, poniendo el foco en las decisiones que deberá tomar el entrenador portugués. El periodista considera que el problema va mucho más allá de elegir una alineación para el próximo encuentro ante el Celta. La convivencia de Vinicius, Mbappé, Bellingham y Diomandé supone un desafío deportivo, pero también de gestión de vestuario, especialmente después de que el conjunto blanco haya encontrado un funcionamiento que parece dar resultados. Pepe Brasín ha recordado que el Real Madrid ha conseguido ocho victorias consecutivas con un protagonismo muy reducido de Vinicius, que se perdió cuatro encuentros de Liga durante ese periodo. Unos resultados que, a su juicio, obligan a analizar si el regreso del brasileño puede alterar el equilibrio conseguido. "Todo lo que ha pasado en este sándwich que hemos vivido entre dos parones de selecciones, esos ocho partidos que ha ganado de manera consecutiva el Real Madrid y en los que Vinicius ha sido actor secundario en el mejor de los casos, abren de par en par un debate que ya estaba abierto", ha explicado. El periodista considera que Mourinho afronta una situación especialmente delicada: "Tiene que hacer un puzzle, un tetris de una complejidad desde el punto de vista deportivo, pero también desde el punto de vista emocional y de la gestión de grupo". No obstante, la buena dinámica del equipo permite afrontar el regreso del brasileño con cierta tranquilidad. "No habrá, creo, ningún incendio si no juega de inicio frente al Celta de Vigo", ha señalado Brasín, que también contempla la posibilidad de repartir descansos entre las principales estrellas del equipo. Una de las grandes incógnitas es si Mourinho podrá encontrar una fórmula para que Vinicius, Mbappé, Bellingham y Diomandé compartan el terreno de juego sin perjudicar el rendimiento colectivo: "Las cuatro hasta ahora nunca han funcionado. Si va a funcionar, está por ver. Y tarde o temprano, el Real Madrid y Mourinho en particular tienen que asumir si eso es lo mejor para el equipo o no", ha reflexionado. Pese a las dificultades, Brasín defiende que los mejores futbolistas deben tener protagonismo para que la plantilla alcance su máximo potencial. "Yo sostengo que para que una plantilla alcance su mejor nivel, los mejores jugadores tienen que estar en el campo. Punto", ha asegurado. El periodista también ha incidido en la responsabilidad del entrenador para encontrar ese equilibrio: "Es ahí donde aparece la mano de un entrenador. El que tiene ese material tiene la necesidad de ver cómo lo encaja". Más allá de las cuestiones tácticas, Brasín ha advertido de las consecuencias que podría tener relegar a Vinicius a un segundo plano dentro del equipo. El brasileño mantiene su condición de estrella mundial y gestionar su protagonismo será una de las grandes responsabilidades de Mourinho: "No puedes tener un jugador que gana 60 millones de euros, una megaestrella mundial en rol secundario. Es imposible", ha afirmado con contundencia. El periodista ha ido todavía más lejos al advertir de los problemas que podría generar esa situación: "Eso no va a pasar, seguro. Porque si eso pasa, va a haber problemas, va a haber un incendio, fijo". Para Brasín, el dilema afecta incluso a la planificación y a la estructura deportiva del Real Madrid. "Este es estructural de club. Este ya no es una cuestión solo de jugar bien, mal o regular, ganar o perder. Es que afecta directamente a toda la idea que ahora mismo emana como club, como plantilla, el Real Madrid de fútbol", ha concluido.

articles.title: Fabian Hurzeler: How Brighton boss won fans over as Seagulls relish in more controlled football
articles.summary: Brighton fans were calling for Fabian Hurzeler to be sacked in February, but a subtle change in approach has the Seagulls among Premier League title contenders; watch Hull vs Brighton live on Sky Sports Premier League and Main Event on Super Sunday; kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
There was scepticism when the German came in at the Amex in 2024 as the youngest permanent head coach in the English top flight. Nearly two and a half years on, that all looks rather silly.

The Seagulls went into the international break perched rather comfortably in second. Paul Merson said in October that if they could beat Liverpool at Anfield and Manchester City at the Etihad, Hurzeler's side would truly be in the title race. They lost on Merseyside, but stunned City in a 1-0 victory .

A 50 per cent return is more than respectable from those two trips. Stay in the hunt throughout Christmas, and there is no doubt that Brighton would have to be viewed as a championship contender.

It's an unbelievable statement, especially considering where Hurzeler found himself earlier this year.

An eight-game winless run throughout January and February heaped pressure on the German and even saw him at times booed by the Amex faithful.

"It's the hardest moment [of my career] but it's also the moment where I learn the most and I will grow the most," Hurzeler emphasised after a 1-0 defeat at home to Crystal Palace in the midst of that torrid streak.

Learn and grow he most certainly did. But in what way has that been the case?

Likened to Jurgen Klopp when he first arrived by former Liverpool midfielder James Milner, Hurzeler's Brighton have actually adopted less of a 'heavy-metal' style this season.

While their distance covered per game is similar to that of last term, their intensity actually seems to be down, averaging far fewer sprints than previously. This isn't a case of Brighton getting lazy, though.

Instead, they are picking and choosing their moments. Setting traps rather than flying around the pitch. The result is a far more efficient performance out of possession. Their interception figures are around the same as they were last season (8.4 per game vs 8.3), and they are forcing more high turnovers.

Thanks to that, Brighton are seeing much more of the ball - only Arsenal, Manchester City and Spurs have a higher possession percentage in the Premier League. Their build-up play is also far less direct and transitional, as the Seagulls have managed more than three extra 10+ passing sequences per game than last season.

They are by no means playing tiki-taka football, but what they are doing is trying to set the tempo on the ball as opposed to off it.

This effects both ends of the pitch. They are already three clean sheets away from matching their Premier League total from last season. They have close to four more shots a game and average slightly over one extra goal.

If there needed to be any more evidence of how the change of approach has worked wonders for Hurzeler all you have to do is look at how Brighton fared when they last faced Crystal Palace.

Just 252 days after "the hardest moment" of his career, he exacts devastating revenge with a 5-0 thrashing of the Eagles. He even had fans pleading for him to stay after being linked with the Manchester United job. Going from hearing your own supporters sing 'sacked in the morning' to that is some turnaround.

Given that Hurzeler was only 31 when appointed, his ideas and tactics were bound to mature over time. Everyone slows down in their old age, right? Admittedly, 33 is far from old, but those two years have certainly given the Texas-born coach more wisdom to play with.

With that, his side now have a new-found sense of control. It has raised the club's stock. It has raised their coach's stock.

Over the last 12-18 months especially, the idea that the work done off the ball is more crucial to success than what is done on it has become more at the forefront of everyone's mind. The famous counter to that is: the best form of defence is attack.

Hurzeler appears to have found a happy medium between those two ideologies. One that still sees his players adopt a modern high press, but now focuses on locking things up defensively by patrolling games on the ball.

The balance is working perfectly. Whether it can be sustained to produce something truly remarkable is anyone's guess. But that shouldn't stop Brighton fans daring to entertain delusions of grandeur.

Europe? Champions League? A Premier League title? The further up you go, the less realistic it feels to say. Yet, from adversity, Hurzeler has Brighton playing in a way that makes it hard to definitively rule them out of the running for any of it.

articles.title: How the story of Dylan Tombides is helping educate FIFA U17 World Cup players about testicular cancer
articles.summary: Mother and brother of former West Ham and Australia youth team striker Dylan Tombides have partnered with FIFA to raise awareness of testicular cancer; Visit dt38.org to find out more about DT38 Foundation, Dylan's story and advice and guidance about testicular cancer.
articles.body:
Tombides passed away in April 2014 aged just 20, following a battle with the cancer he was diagnosed with while on international duty with Australia's youth team in Mexico in 2011.

A random drugs test revealed what had originally been misdiagnosed by his GP as a cyst was far more serious. Three years of "really intense chemotherapy" followed, says his mother Tracy.

The DT38 Foundation was set up in his name and, in partnership with FIFA Medical, Tracy and Dylan's brother Taylor are part of the initiative at this year's tournament in Doha to explain to players why regular self-examination matters and how to carry it out.

"Getting the call from FIFA was a massive opportunity and an amazing thing for us and for the charity," says Taylor. "Obviously, it's where Dylan last kind of played healthy before his diagnosis. So to come back to where it all started for us as a family is a grateful honour."

During two weeks of talks to 48 teams, Tracy and Taylor have presented to 1,200 players.

With testicular cancer the most common cancer in males aged 15 to 44 - but highly treatable and in most cases curable when detected early - the importance of the sessions could be life changing.

"It's the number one cause of fatality of cancer in this particular age group," explains Dr Andy Massey, FIFA's Medical Director, who helped form the partnership and has overseen the provision of free scans to players during the tournament.

"This is one of the biggest things I think I've ever done in my sports medicine career because it has such a reach."

Tracy and Taylor's accounts of Dylan's stories have had a powerful impact on their audiences.

"One of the young players stood in front of me and said, 'I'm so sorry for your loss. I'm sorry your son isn't coming home to you. We are so grateful that you are telling us all about it'," says Tracy, recounting a talk with the Jamaican team. A similarly emotional conversation with the French squad ended in hugs instead of handshakes.

The DT38 Foundation have a campaign called Check One Two, encouraging men to check themselves on the first day of every month. Dylan's nickname 'Didge' also provides an acronym and hashtag for the foundation: Delay Is Deadly, Get Educated.

"Early detection is the difference between dealing with cancer treatment that has a 96 per cent cure rate or the figures drop away very, very quickly if you have to go to round two or round three of chemotherapy," says Tracy, who also encourages men with concerns to "insist on an ultrasound" test.

Tracy and Taylor treasure "messages that we've got from people who say, 'I thought of Dylan's story when I found a lump and I knew not to delay. I had testicular cancer and now I'm cancer-free and Dylan saved my life'."

"That tells us that what we're doing is life-changing for that family, that person," says Tracy.

Taylor believes they can have an impact through generations, too. "The effect is lasting. If we can teach these kids now, we know the next generation, they'll teach their kids and they'll teach their kids and it'll be continuous," he says.

"We're not just affecting one life, we're affecting a whole generation of lives, which is the biggest part of it. Without FIFA, we couldn't touch as many people as we have."

Visit dt38.org to find out more about the DT38 Foundation, Dylan's story and advice and guidance about testicular cancer.

articles.title: Manchester United: Drone operator removes footage of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session and apologises
articles.summary: A 12-minute video of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session at Manchester United was leaked online, showing the new head coach doing training drills ahead of Sunday's match against Liverpool, live on Sky; the apologetic drone operator says he has now taken down the footage
articles.body:
The 12-minute drone footage over United's Carrington training ground showed the the Argentine overseeing various tactical drills with his new team as they prepared for their game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, live on Sky Sports .

CC Overview, who posted the footage, said on Friday morning: "I would like to speak about yesterday's incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part. My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time.

"I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

"I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets. I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.

"I would also like to state that Liverpool Football Club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday. The video has been removed from my channel.

"I have spent the past four years building up my YouTube channel and were well regarded in the fields I film and would now like to get back to building up my damaged reputation and making well-received responsible videos. Thank you."

However, the video has now been shared widely across social media. The footage has been viewed over eight million times on reposts from other X accounts and has since been reuploaded by several other YouTube channels, collectively attracting hundreds of thousands of views.

United have signs around the Carrington area warning that the use of drones is "strictly prohibited" and anyone caught "will be reported for prosecution and subject to civil action".

After the video emerged on Thursday evening, CC Overview maintained they had not broken any laws and claimed there were "many other media there".

However, the training was a closed session and not open to the media. Manchester United declined to comment when contacted by Sky Sports News .

'Pochettino must now protect his players from another story'

"This is quite an incredible story… this was a drone operator who flew not necessarily over the training ground or over Carrington, but far enough with a zoom that could really detail the tactical set-up that maybe Pochettino will go with on Sunday or what he's certainly working towards.

"You could also see the personnel who were there, questions around some players' fitness or availability… which ones were in place in his tactics run-through as well.

"This is a huge disappointment and not ideal for this Manchester United team who are trying to build some momentum, find some positive energy going into Pochettino's first game against Liverpool.

"It's just one win in 11 games in all competitions, and they're now having to get through another story and another burden.

"For Pochettino, it is now about protecting this group of players from more negative energy around them.

"Even before this happened, these types of incidents have been a concern for teams across the Premier League and EFL. Other clubs will be very aware and start thinking about how they can protect themselves from this happening to them.

"The footage has now been deleted, but of course it's across all social media platforms and you can't really take it back once it is out there, can you?"

'Difficult to stop this behaviour' claims drone expert

Drone expert Jon Hurndall speaking with Sky Sports News:

"The only way to stop it is to reduce the airspace in the open category, which I guess the operator has been operating in. There's not much they can do. All the signage in the world isn't going to stop the operator from flying over.

"My view on it is that the privacy is there to stop people filming into homes. It's more of a legal debate as to whether filming a training session breaches privacy laws.

"There's lots of different sections of the law and the regulations. This guy seems to be operating in the open category.

"There's different certifications of aircraft. Different weight categories. The fundamentals are that when you're operating in a certain category you can't fly over assemblies of people.

"I don't know if that's the case here, but an assembly of people would be a group who can't move out of the way in the event of failure. On a sporadic training pitch, it's difficult to to say that a rule's been breached. Then once you're up in the air, you're in the realms of airspace. If there is no airspace restriction in that particular area and you're not near an airport, it's pretty difficult to stop that type of behaviour.

"I think the only way to stop it from happening is to increase security. Maybe buy more land because they can only go a maximum 500 metres away from the eyeline of the pilot. They have to remain within the view of the system in the air.

"If that's not a possibility, the only thing is to really restrict the airspace. That's up to the CAA (Civil Aviation Authority) on if they will allow that."

articles.title: Mourinho: "Aquí no hay privilegios y nadie juega por decreto
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Real Madrid insiste en que Vinicius puede ser decisivo y destaca el valor que tiene en el grupo, pero no garantiza el puesto a nadie
articles.summary: El entrenador del Real Madrid insiste en que Vinicius puede ser decisivo y destaca el valor que tiene en el grupo, pero no garantiza el puesto a nadie
articles.body: José Mourinho sabía lo que le esperaba. Un regreso de Vinicius tras cuatro partidos de sanción, la mejoría ostensible sin él para afianzar la racha y los cinco goles del brasileño con Brasil formaban un cóctel bien explosivo. Por eso soltó lo que soltó en la primera pregunta de la ronda que siempre corre a cargo del canal oficial del club. "Gracias por la única pregunta sobre el partido", dijo. Mou dejó claro que nadie en la plantilla tiene el puesto asegurado, insistió en el concepto equivocado de los medios del once titular para hablar de una plantilla capaz de resistir el calendario. Insistió también que espera al mejor Vinicius y se marchó con un frío comentario del adiós de Cristiano de Portugal. El partido de mañana: "gracias por la única pregunta sobre el partido. El Celta es mucho mejor de los puntos que tiene, ya nos ganó la temporada pasada, están jugando en Europa y quizá eso les está quitando algunos puntos, pero mañana este factor no existe. El equipo ha tenido tiempo para trabajar estas dos semanas. Encajan pocos goles porque son muy organizados y es un partido muy importante para nosotros. Hemos estado mucho tiempo fuera del Bernabéu pero lo hemos hecho bien. Hoy es el primer día que tenemos a todos juntos, pero estamos bien y la gente está feliz de volver a estar junta". La vuelta de Vinicius y lo que dijo sobre su escasa preparación tras el Mundial: "ahora es invierno y es este periodo el que nos interesa. Ya ha pasado el verano y por lo tanto tengo poco que decir a las declaraciones de Vini. Entramos en una etapa difícil con tres competiciones, después viene la Supercopa, está claro que queremos un buen Vinicius y es lo que esperamos". El Madrid mejora físicamente y menos lesiones: "los jugadores se lesionan menos... hasta ahora, no podemos prever el futuro, lo principal es el modo en que los jugadores piensan y sienten su profesión, en cómo trabajan y recuperan y se entregan a las herramientas de trabajo que tenemos. Crédito total para los jugadores, lo de estar bien físicamente es una cosa multifactorial, como cuando se está mal no es solo por el físico, el bien y el mal es multifactorial. Hemos tenido buenos resultados y es también factorial, hay un buen grupo y cuando podemos trabajar lo hacemos bien, hay buena comunicación y tenemos nuestras dificultades. Recuerdo las dos derrotas que hemos tenido y el ambiente que hemos vivido juntos y no era muy diferente a lo de ahora". Cómo se recupera a Vini, como titular o desde el banquillo: "Titular, en el banquillo, en la grada... da igual. Es algo extraño porque hace un par de semanas Vini era el problema gigante y después de marcar con Brasil hablamos de si juega o no, si tiene que jugar, creo que es demasiado. Lo que digo ahora ya lo dije, es un jugador increíble, lo queremos y lo necesitamos, le ayudamos y no hay jugadores aquí con privilegios. Nadie tiene que jugar por decreto, son jugadores que trabajan. El Madrid tiene que tener una plantilla fuerte, con muchos jugadores buenos, y esa historia de juega o no juega... Hay 23 jugadores o más que me van a obligar a dejar jugadores en la grada y es la vida que yo quiero para el Madrid y es diferente a vuestro trabajo. No quiero once jugadores buenos, quiero muchos". JJ Gabriel: "No tengo nada que decir, no tengo feeling con los jugadores con los que cuento y no trabajan conmigo". El futuro de Endrick: "Está muy bien aquí, para mí el Madrid es más importante que Endrick. Le quiero mucho y tengo mucho cariño por él, le necesito, ya tienes la respuesta, a los clubes, a los agentes, después el Madrid decide una cosa diferente, hay que respetar. Pero yo y el Madrid sabemos que es importante". Güler; "Son todos importantes, no quiero decir que la evolución en su juego es por mí, es algo natural de un niño a un hombre, de un super talento y que hace cosas que nunca había hecho". Las declaraciones de Vinicius: "ya ha pasado, verano e invierno, calor y frío. Ha pasado el impacto del Mundial, ha pasado una etapa de un chico, no deja de ser un chico a esa edad que ha hecho su autoanálisis, a lo mejor podría no haberlo dicho, pero no me gusta nunca criticar la apertura. Ahora vamos a llegar, espero, a una situación en la Champions con cruces, donde cada punto en Liga que se gana será decisivo, y es ahí que Vini puede hacer la diferencia, con la experiencia que ya tiene y ser decisivo en el momento decisivo, el jugador que todos quieren en el vestuario, Vini es uno de ellos, del vestuario, y está muy empeñado en volver a ser decisivo en el Madrid como ha sido muchos años". El adiós de Cristiano de Portugal: "como portugués quiero que Portugal gane siempre, después, me lavo las manos y no hablo". Qué destaca de este grupo con respecto al de la primera etapa: "No me pidas comparar... Era un grupo que lo ha dado todo. Que por circunstancias de mi momento, la relación en la última temporada se ha ido transformando. Pero más que esto, mi feeling es que el perfil que había metido como entrenador y líder... el trabajo ya estaba hecho. Y era mejor para el club una nueva etapa, con un entrenador con un perfil distinto. El club no pudo haber elegido mejor el entrenador que me sucedió. Fui a Inglaterra y ha ido muy bien para todos. Pero no quiero comparar grupos. Los dos eran súper talentosos, con jugadores de alto nivel. Pero este es el Real Madrid. Temporada tras temporada y generación tras generación".

articles.title: Stoke City v Birmingham City: Third meets first in Championship
articles.summary: Stoke host Birmingham in a Championship game of two teams both bang in form going into the latest international break. How will they re-emerge?
articles.body:
Stoke City v Birmingham City: Third v first in the Championship.

That is a "tale of two cities" that did not look too likely to get written when Mark Robins' Potters started this season with three straight defeats and Blues won only two of their first eight league games under Chris Davies.

But, just like you should never judge a book by its cover, the footballing equivalent is to never judge any league table until after 10 games.

The season is now three months old - after Saturday's meeting at the Bet365 Stadium it will be more than a third of the way in.

And a clearer picture is starting to emerge as to whether what was once the "worst of times", especially in Stoke's case, might yet become the "best of times" before this 46-game campaign ends.

With 15 games gone, there are three clubs right at the top all on 29 points in what is already looking a ridiculously tight Championship table .

And two of them meet head on in front of an expected full house in the Potteries, having both been bang in form going into the latest international break.

Stoke are on a run of nine wins and only one defeat in 12 league games since the start of September, while Blues have won six out of seven since football returned after the first autumn international break.

So, how will things start to shape up after the second such break?

EFL preview: Evans' gripes & unexpected departures

'One of most physical XIs in league' - Davies on Stoke

Stoke had the edge last season, winning 1-0 at home in September before drawing 1-1 in the return at St Andrew's in January, prior to Blues going into their late-season decline - and Davies can see the difference in the Potters.

"I watched the game back from when we played them a year ago and it looks very different," the Blues boss told BBC Radio WM.

"He [Mark Robins] has made a big impact from where they were last season. A real stamp of his identity.

"They've gone to a back five and, since then, they've conceded the fewest goals in the league - nine in 12 games.

"They've looked strong, particularly in the central areas. They've got bigger. They're now one of the most physical starting XIs in the league."

While extolling the Potters' defensive qualities, Davies is also well aware they have an attacking threat and he is an admirer of Stoke's American winger Jack McGlynn, who is their top scorer with five goals.

"I already knew a little bit about the boy McGlynn," said Davies. "He's been exceptional with the goals he's got.

"They're a team much like ourselves. I want us to go there as a measure to see how far we've come, if we can display what we've been showing recently."

'They've got some real talent' - Robins on Blues

Stoke boss Mark Robins' main concern is determining the fitness of his international contingent, having had 10 out of his 20-man matchday squad from their 2-1 win at Portsmouth away for almost a fortnight.

Of the 14 players involved that day, Swedish keeper Viktor Johansson, Bosun Lawal (Ireland), Robert Bozenik (Slovenia), Luke Graham (Scotland) and euphoric Northern Ireland pair Ethan Galbraith and Justin Devenny all played, while McGlynn was part of new Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino's USA send-off.

"They've changed a little bit," Robins told BBC Midlands Today. "They've clearly taken a lot from the Championship last season.

"They've got some players in form and some coming back from international duty, although less than we have.

"A lot [of their players] have been together a few seasons now - and they've got some real talent. But it gives us a chance to pit ourselves against the team at the top. The last time we did that was against Charlton ."

Having already seen off one table-topping team in the Potteries this season, Robins is not getting carried away though.

"It's nice to be where we are," he added. "We've never been in the conversation before and we want to be in that conversation."

Stoke will hold a minute's applause before the game to mark the recent passings of Potters legend Peter Dobing and former manager Gudjon Thordarson.

'Blues taking risks, Stoke resilient' - old boy Clarkson

One local celebrity fan looking forward to Saturday's game more than most is a man with a foot in both camps - ex-Birmingham and Stoke full-back Ian Clarkson.

Boyhood Blues fan Clarkson made 174 appearances for the club between 1988 and 1993, when he moved on to Stoke, where he made a further 95 appearances.

After seeing out his career with Northampton Town, Kidderminster Harriers and Nuneaton Borough, Clarkson, now 55, then took his talents into the press box, reporting on Blues first for the Express & Star then the Birmingham Post - and he now coaches football in his teaching role at Repton College.

He has seen plenty of both clubs this season - and both have taken him slightly by surprise.

"Blues are a lot more inclined to attack than they were last season, they look more likely to take a few risks," Clarkson told BBC Sport.

"The signing of August Priske in January is obviously starting to reap rewards and it's bringing the best out of Jay Stansfield. Plus you've got good contributions coming from their wingers and two more on the bench to come on.

"Blues are playing some lovely football right now. Chris Davies is obviously a manager who works very hard at it. And they just seem to have got it right. They've clicked."

"Stoke are starting to look more like a Stoke City team, in the nicest possible way.

"Mark Robins is just one of those managers who, wherever he is, just seems to get better. The longer he stays at a club the better he gets. And they really do look far more resilient.

"There's something about the place that just feels different this season. They've got the fans back on side and that's more important than anything. Everyone knows how tough a place Stoke can be when it's bouncing."

As to who will win on Saturday? And where they might be come season's end?

"It's way too early to be talking in those terms," added Clarkson. "Let's be honest, I'm a Blues fan, so in any season I'd want Blues to finish top, then Stoke second. And they've both made great starts. But it's too soon to say. There's a long, long way to go."

articles.title: NWSL doesn’t have a problem with political activism - as long as it agrees with the stance
articles.summary: The NWSL faces questions over fan conduct after "Save Women's Sports" protesters were removed from a Portland Thorns game amid fan backlash.
articles.body: Agitators. Anti-trans. Hateful. Bad-faith aisle-blockers. This is how readers of The Athletic were introduced to peaceful protesters advocating for the separation of biological males and females in sports at National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) games. The story ran Thursday following a press conference held by NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman ahead of Saturday's league championship game in Washington, D.C. NWSL BOSS SAYS ALL FANS ARE 'WELCOME' AHEAD OF FINAL AFTER MULTIPLE EJECTIONS OF WOMEN'S SPORTS ADVOCATES Among the topics? How the league intends to handle political expression in its stadiums. Well, at least the kind it doesn't like. Last month, a group of about 20 protesters wearing XX-XY Athletics apparel were forcibly removed from a Portland Thorns game after unfurling a banner reading "Save Women's Sports." Their ejections came after fans from the Thorns' supporters' section obscured their banner with transgender pride flags, hurled a flurry of F-bombs in their direction, allegedly jabbed them with flagpoles and sent one woman tumbling over two rows of seats. So who were the aggressors? Judging by the actions of security personnel at Providence Park, it was the "Save Women's Sports" crowd. The Athletic columnist and NWSL commissioner seem to agree. The headline for Thursday's piece was "As NWSL addresses anti-trans protests, setting clear fan expectations should be top priority." It echoed the familiar media trope that anyone who believes biological females should have their own spaces in sports is automatically "anti-trans." The column highlighted Berman's effusive praise of the league's supporters' groups and the distinction she drew between fans there for the soccer and those there for the politics. EXCLUSIVE: DOJ REVIEWING PORTLAND THORNS INCIDENT SHOWING WOMEN’S SPORTS SUPPORTERS STRUCK, FORCIBLY REMOVED "As we think about the environment we create in our stadiums, we want to make sure that everybody understands and knows our fan code of conduct," Berman said after calling the supporters' groups the "lifeblood" of the NWSL. "We expect the people who come into our buildings, no matter their points of view, to be there to enjoy the excitement and the incredible athleticism of our players and the competition on the field. If people are there for that reason, they are 100 percent welcome." I'm not going to pretend that the "Save Women's Sports" protesters were as passionate about soccer as the Rose City Riveters — the Thorns' main supporters' group. But anyone who thinks the Riveters are just a bunch of 9-to-5ers looking to get lost in the beautiful game for 90 minutes is as naive as the guy who thinks the hot girl in the group photo was the one who swiped right on him. At times, these supporters' sections look more like political rallies than soccer crowds. You'll see Black Lives Matter signs. You'll see "Protect Trans Youth" shirts with knives on them. You'll see a "F—K Trump" scarf or an Iron Front flag — a symbol commonly associated with Antifa. And while there's no doubt the XX-XY Athletics crowd was there to gain visibility — particularly ahead of multiple state ballot initiatives aimed at preserving female-only sports — it wasn't the protesters behaving like maniacs in Portland. Judge for yourself in the video below. Or this one. Despite that, the writer described the XX-XY types as "agitators," embedded a Bluesky post calling them "hateful folks" and cited anonymous sources claiming the protesters were removed because they were blocking aisles. One of the videos above shows supporters doing the aisle-blocking. Who's working in "bad faith" again? FORMER NWSL PLAYER SAYS LEAGUE CULTURE PRESSURED ATHLETES TO SUPPORT POLITICAL MESSAGES THEY OPPOSED As the column notes, Portland wasn't the only NWSL stop for the "Save Women's Sports" crowd. A similar protest at a Seattle Reign game drew considerably fewer participants — just four protesters, according to The Athletic. They, too, were immediately surrounded by fans wielding transgender pride flags and were eventually escorted out of the stadium by those fans. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Athletic column also notes that the NWSL's fan code of conduct prohibits displays advocating for or against political candidates or legislation. But I wonder how many people have been bounced from NWSL games for sporting an anti-Trump scarf. Look, if Berman wants to rid NWSL stadiums of political expression and make these games exclusively about soccer, that's fine. If she wants to foster an environment where fans are free to express their political views, that's fine, too. But spare us the notion that the people waving transgender pride flags are there strictly for the soccer while the people wearing XX-XY shirts are there strictly for the politics. The issue isn't that politics have infiltrated the NWSL. It's that one brand of politics gets you cheers while another gets you chucked. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP What do you think of the NWSL's stance? Let me know at Matthew.calkins@outkick.com

articles.summary: The ESPN College Gameday crew is back on the road for a Week 12 match-up between two rival schools that dates back decades.
articles.body:
The ESPN College Gameday crew is back on the road for a Week 12 match-up between two rival schools that dates back decades.

What campus is welcoming the premier college football pregame show and when can viewers check out all of the coverage?

Find out in this preview of Saturday's show.

Location: Lakeside Patio at University of Miami

Crew: Rece Davis, Kirk Herbstreit, Desmond Howard, Nick Saban, Pat McAfee, Jess Sims, Jen Lada, "Stanford" Steve Coughlin, Pete Thamel

Celebrity Guest Picker: Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson

Virginia Tech arrives in Miami on the heels of an embarrassing loss to the Stanford Cardinal, and just over a month removed from another terrible loss to the California Golden Bears.

The Miami Hurricanes are 20.5-point favorites in Saturday night's match-up, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and things may prove uglier than that by the time the final whistle sounds.

The Hurricanes are, statistically, beneath the Hokies defensively, but if Stanford were able to force three turnovers against James Franklin's squad, expect a faster, nastier Hurricanes unit to prove problematic for quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer and crew.

Miami signal-caller Darian Mensah is one of the best passers in the game and a Heisman contender who should find success against the Hokies' defense. Completing 76.3 percent of his passes, with 29 touchdowns and two interceptions, he is going to find the end zone, and he will not make many mistakes along the way.

He will be without leading receiver Malachi Toney, but that will not be enough to derail the Hurricanes' explosive offense.

This one will be over by halftime and if not, definitely at some point early in the third quarter and the Hurricanes physically overwhelm Virginia Tech, their hopes and dreams of a College Football National Championship still alive, despite their loss to Notre Dame two weeks ago.

Virginia Tech will find some plays courtesy of an overly aggressive Miami defense, and may keep it close early, but superior talent will prevail and the blowout will be on.

articles.title: The 10 Biggest 5-Star Recruiting Busts of the Past Decade
articles.summary: The excitement of landing a 5-star prospect is hard to forget.
articles.body:
The excitement of landing a 5-star prospect is hard to forget.

For a coaching staff, the signature is the product of many phone calls, text messages, visits and other contacts. That top-ranked talent is the source of hope, optimism and dreams all over the fanbase.

Unfortunately, some recruits became hard to forget for a different reason: They just never panned out.

The following players had very little production at the Football Bowl Subdivision level. It's important to remember someone like Arch Manning—though he's fallen short of championship expectations as of this writing—has been a net-positive player at Texas. Disappointment is far different from a bust .

Additionally, there are several players at risk of joining this inglorious list still on rosters in 2026. The narrative isn't great for Bryce Underwood or Malachi Nelson, for example. But we won't say those stories are finished quite yet.

Five-stars are based on the final 247Sports Composite Rankings in each cycle.

Considered the No. 5 overall prospect in the 2019 class, Antonio Alfano enrolled at Alabama as the next great pass-rusher for the powerhouse program.

Alfano left Alabama early as a freshman while struggling with family matters. After transferring to Colorado, he dealt with off-field issues along with health challenges—epilepsy, specifically—that further derailed his career.

Later, he returned to play at Lackawanna College (JUCO) and appeared in four games with the Edmonton Elks of the Canadian Football League.

Calvin Ashley is a prime example of why criteria matters.

From an overall football view, he wouldn't necessarily fit "bust" status. Even if only briefly, Ashley spent part of the summer of 2021 with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He earned All-USFL honors with the New Jersey Generals in 2023.

But those highlights came beyond the FBS, the level at which Auburn anticipated an immense impact from the 2017 cycle's No. 26 player.

Over two seasons on the Plains, he made six appearances, including one start.

Ashley transferred to Florida Atlantic in early 2019 but soon joined the FCS program at Florida A&M to be closer to his newborn son. He played one season at FAMU.

Speedy wide receiver Jurrion Dickey , the headliner of Oregon's 2023 recruiting class, arrived on campus as the nation's No. 22 overall prospect.

However, he hardly made an impact in his two-plus seasons with the Ducks. Dickey notched a seven-yard catch in the Fiesta Bowl as a true freshman and a seven-yard reception in a rout of Michigan State in 2024. That was the full extent of his production at Oregon.

Oregon suspended him indefinitely prior to the 2025 season for violating team rules. He left for a junior college shortly thereafter.

Dickey has since become a productive target for NAIA school Midland University.

Throughout six years at LSU, a long list of setbacks cost John Emery Jr. an opportunity to become a core contributor.

Ranked 13th in his class, Emery held a reserve role on the iconic 2019 championship team. Emery managed 451 scrimmage yards in 2020, but he missed the 2021 season due to academic ineligibility.

Emery returned in 2022 and shared the backfield with two others, managing 375 yards and six scores on the ground.

He remained buried on the depth chart in 2023. A torn right ACL ended his brutal season in November. Most cruelly, he earned the starting nod in 2024 but made a single appearance before a torn left ACL ended the year.

Emery transferred to UTSA in 2025 but handled just four carries in one game.

It had to be Washington for Sam Huard . Where else could he go?

Damon Huard, his father, left the program in 1995 as its all-time leader in career passing yards. Brock Huard, Sam's uncle, replaced his brother and broke that record, along with many others.

So, when the nation's 12th-ranked prospect headed to Washington in 2021, expectations were a continuation of the family legacy.

Huard started one game as a true freshman, tossing four interceptions in a loss to rival Washington State. He spent 2022 as UW's third-stringer, transferred to FCS Cal Poly in 2023, returned to the FBS with Utah in 2024 but didn't play, and then watched from the sideline at USC in 2025.

The one exception during his time at USC? Throwing a fourth-down pass as part of a clever, controversial trick play that resulted in a Big Ten rule change.

Particularly on the heels of Thaddeus Moss being so productive on the 2019 championship team, Arik Gilbert went to LSU with a tremendous outlook.

LSU needed to address Moss' void at tight end. Gilbert, an imposing 6'5", 253-pounder ranked fifth in his class, had a clear path to immediate playing time and took advantage. He reeled in 35 passes for 368 yards and two touchdowns as a true freshman in 2020 for the Tigers.

From there, though, off-field issues wrecked his college career.

Gilbert transferred to Georgia but didn't play in 2021 due to personal reasons. He mustered two catches for 16 yards and a touchdown, then bolted for Nebraska, where he never entered a game.

In 2015, UCLA landed its QB of the future in 5-star Josh Rosen . One year later, the Bruins landed the cornerstone of their defense in Mique Juarez , the No. 11 recruit in the cycle.

Juarez immediately felt the weight of that pressure and stepped away from the team during fall practices. He returned for the 2017 season, contributing on special teams and making three tackles.

During the 2018 opener, a concussion stalled Juarez's progress. He missed the rest of the year, and he left UCLA after being told he shouldn't play football again.

Juarez chose Utah as a transfer destination but never appeared on the roster.

In the moment, it seemed like Lorenzo Lingard appeared at the perfect time for Miami. The program had begun to ascend as Mark Richt put his alma mater back on the national radar and also snapped a long streak of losing bowl games.

Lingard, the No. 25 player in the 2018 class, would be the next great running back at a school known for producing them.

The vision never became reality at a prominent spot.

After logging 17 carries as a freshman before a knee injury ended his year, Lingard only played a couple of games on special teams in 2019. He transferred to Florida, where he managed 27 touches over three seasons.

Lingard at least salvaged one fine campaign at Akron in 2023, totaling 1,009 scrimmage yards for the 2-10 Zips.

"As a freshman at Alabama, I do plan on winning the Heisman, nothing less," Trey Sanders said on signing day in 2019.

Why wouldn't the No. 6 prospect of the cycle be confident? Between his physical stature and versatility as a pass-catcher, he'd been labeled college-ready. And he was headed to Alabama, a major NFL pipeline at the position.

However, both on- and off-field injuries halted Sanders' dream.

That first season, a foot injury shelved him. Sanders returned in 2020 before a car accident ended his campaign. Though he collected 314 yards in 2021, a majority of his carries happened in the second half of lopsided games.

Over three seasons with the Crimson Tide, he turned 125 offensive touches into 594 scrimmage yards. He then totaled 242 yards in two years at TCU.

Saquon Barkley. Miles Sanders. Ricky Slade .

Upon his arrival in 2018, it was the dream backfield progression for a rising program. Slade, who ranked 27th overall in that cycle, had an opportunity to immediately impact the Nittany Lions.

Slade served as the backup in his freshman year, rushing for 257 yards and six touchdowns. He won the starting job in 2019, yet tumbled in a four-player rotation, managing 319 scrimmage yards before electing to transfer.

At the time, it made sense. Slade followed his offensive coordinator, Ricky Rahne, to Old Dominion with the potential to become the featured runner. However, the school canceled its 2020 season amidst the COVID-19 pandemic.

Slade was no longer part of the ODU roster by February 2021 and didn't play elsewhere.

articles.title: Southampton boss Tonda Eckert given contract extension despite 'Spygate' controversy
articles.summary: Southampton were expelled from the Championship play-offs in May after admitting to "multiple breaches" of unauthorised filming of their opponents' training; club stuck by their manager Tonda Eckert and now have given him a new contract
articles.body:
Saints were kicked out of the Championship play-off final and docked four points this season having admitted three breaches of EFL regulations after being caught spying on semi-final opponents Middlesbrough and two other teams.

Eckert accepted full responsibility and was charged by the FA with three breaches of Rule E3.1 in relation to "misconduct", which hung over Southampton and their manager heading into the new campaign.

However, the club has stuck by their man with Southampton owner Dragan Solak saying at the time of the punishment: "We are confident the manager has learned from this matter, and a suspended sentence allows him to continue in his role."

Despite a four point deduction, Southampton sit five points off top spot in the Sky Bet Championship. Saints are also unbeaten in their last 17 home league matches, with Eckert suffering only one Championship defeat at St Mary's throughout his tenure to date.

Group Sporting Director Johannes Spors said: "I think it's a great commitment from both sides; from the club to Tonda, and from Tonda to the club. I'm very happy that we have achieved this agreement before the end of the international window, allowing us to go into the busy schedule that is ahead of us with clarity.

"Tonda is very talented and very precise with a great analytical brain, but also has the personality and authority that you need, even at a young age. It is very clear that this is the right place for him, and I'm very happy that he feels that too."

Eckert said: "We've had some conversations that started a couple of weeks ago, and the goal was always clear: to show the same commitment that we have had for the last 12 months. I'm very happy that we have come to the point that we can make it official now.

"There is a lot that has happened in the last 12 months, but the commitment from the club, from Dragan, Johannes and Phil, and the supporters, means everything to me. I am very grateful for that. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through - there is a lot more to come."

May 7: Middlesbrough make formal complaint to the EFL alleging a Southampton member of staff spied on their training session three days before their Championship play-off semi-final first leg.

May 9: Boro boss Kim Hellberg accuses Southampton of cheating after the first leg ends in a 0-0 draw at the Riverside Stadium.

May 12: Southampton charged with a breach of EFL regulations in relation to the spying accusations. Southampton request additional time to conduct an internal review.

The play-off semi-final second leg is played at St Mary's. Shea Charles' extra-time winner earns Southampton a 2-1 victory and a place in the Championship play-off final.

Emotional Hellberg hits out at "disgraceful spying", before Saints boss Tonda Eckert storms out of his press conference after being asked: "Are you a cheat?"

May 13: Photos allegedly showing the Southampton analyst near Middlesbrough's training ground released publicly.

May 14: It is announced the independent hearing to determine Southampton's fate will take place on or before Tuesday May 19. In a statement, the EFL say "the outcome of the disciplinary proceedings may yet result in changes to the fixture."

May 15: Middlesbrough publicly call for Southampton's expulsion from the play-offs. In a statement, they said: "In these circumstances, the only appropriate response is a sporting sanction which would prevent Southampton FC from participating in the EFL Championship play-off final."

May 18: Middlesbrough players return to training as the outcome of the independent disciplinary hearing nears.

May 19: EFL announces Southampton expelled from play-off final after hearing.

May 21: FA confirm they will begin their own investigation into Spygate.

May 23: Middlesbrough lose 1-0 to Hull City in the Championship play-off final.

June 1: WhatsApp messages reveal Eckert "loved" spying information despite the concerns of junior members of Southampton staff.

June 2: Eckert takes full responsibility for Spygate as Southampton owner Dragan Solak backs head coach.

June 17: Eckert tells Sky Sports News he received police protection amid threats during Spygate.

July 22: FA charges Southampton head coach Eckert with three breaches of rule E3.1.

September 25: Eckert is given a suspended six-week ban, running until the end of the 2027/28 season, and a fine.

November 20: Eckert signs new Southampton contract after strong start to the season.

The 33-year-old German's existing deal was expiring at the end of this season after being handed the role permanently last December.

Eckert's future was thrown into doubt over the summer, having been at the centre of an investigation by the Football Association over his role in the 'Spygate' scandal.

Last season, Eckert led the Saints from 21st in the table to a fourth-placed finish after taking over from the sacked Will Still, also making it to the FA Cup semi-final where they took the lead before being knocked-out by Manchester City.

They were set to face Hull City in the play-off final before being thrown out after admitting they spied on three clubs during the Championship season including Middlesbrough.

Real Madrid have announced the extension of Thibaut Courtois' contract with the club until the summer of 2028.

Per Realmadrid.com Real Madrid C.F. and Thibaut Courtois have agreed to extend our player's contract, which ties him to the club until June 30, 2028.

Thibaut Courtois joined Real Madrid in 2018. In his nine seasons wearing our jersey, he has played 348 matches and won 14 titles: 2 Champions League titles, 3 Club World Cups, 2 UEFA Super Cups, 3 La Liga titles, 1 Copa del Rey, and 3 Spanish Super Cups.

His contribution to all these titles has been marked by decisive performances that have established him as the best goalkeeper in the world.

Courtois is 34 years old but is arguably the world's best goalkeeper, so this one-year extension makes sense.

articles.summary: Liverpool host Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday when the Premier League returns from the international break.All eyes will be on Man Utd for the game,...
articles.body:
Liverpool host Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday when the Premier League returns from the international break.

All eyes will be on Man Utd for the game, with Mauricio Pochettino taking charge of the Red Devils for the first time. The Argentine replaced Michael Carrick in the dugout, and has a hard task on his hands. Man Utd are in the relegation zone with just one win from their 10 games, and are winless in eight.

Things are much better for Liverpool under Andoni Iraola. The Reds sit fourth in the Premier League with five wins from 10, though they have struggled to get results at Anfield. Liverpool have won just one of their five home league games this season, with two draws and two defeats.

And they go into this game winless in their past three matches against Man Utd. The Red Devils did the league double over their rivals last season, including a 2-1 win at Anfield.

Iraola will be happy with how the international break when for his Liverpool side. The Reds look to have come through the fixtures unscathed, and there could be returns for two of their previously injured players.

Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong have both returned to training in the buildup to this game, having missed the past one and three games, respectively. Virgil van Dijk is also in training having missed Netherlands duty due to a knock.

Only Van Dijk is likely to start of that Dutch trio, retaining his space in the defence alongside Jeremy Jacquet. Iraola may opt to field an unchanged lineup from the team that started the win over Crystal Palace before the break. Ronald Araujo is expected to continue at right-back, allowing Frimpong time to ease back into the match.

Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister have built a good partnership as the first-choice double pivot, while Liverpool's front four looks pretty settled. Alexander Isak should lead the line with Florian Wirtz behind him, flanked by Cody Gakpo and Bradley Barcola.

Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike and Conor Bradley are longer-term absentees.

Pochettino is unlikely to make any drastic changes for his first Man Utd lineup. The former United States boss will have only had a few days in charge of the Red Devils after officially taking over from Carrick on Wednesday. But there could be one or two changes.

Luke Shaw could return from injury and may go straight into the starting XI, having worked with Pochettino at Southampton. As a result, Diogo Dalot can switch back over to the right, with Noussair Mazraoui dropping out. Another change to the defence might see Lisandro Martinez return to the lineup after his suspension. Harry Maguire faces a late fitness test but should be fine to start.

The rest of the Man Utd team is likely to stay the same from the draw with Aston Villa. With Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte injured, Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo are the go-to double pivot. Bryan Mbeumo is expected to lead the line in the absence of Benjamin Sesko. As a result, Amad Diallo will continue on the right, with Matheus Cunha on the left and Bruno Fernandes in the No.10.
